verses.textZh: 以下是传道者，就是在耶路撒冷作王、大卫的儿子所说的话。
verses.textZhCnvs: 以下是传道者，就是在耶路撒冷作王、大卫的儿子所说的话。
verses.textZhCuv: 在耶路撒冷作王、大卫的儿子、传道者的言语。
verses.textEnNiv: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:
verses.textEnEsv: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNlt: These are the words of the Teacher, King David’s son, who ruled in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:

verses.textZh: 传道者说：虚空的虚空。 虚空的虚空，一切都是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 传道者说：虚空的虚空。 虚空的虚空，一切都是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 传道者说：虚空的虚空， 虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Utterly meaningless! Everything is meaningless."
verses.textEnEsv: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities! All is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: "Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher; "Vanity of vanities, all is vanity."
verses.textEnNlt: "Everything is meaningless," says the Teacher, "completely meaningless!"
verses.textEnNasb: "Futility of futilities," says the Preacher, "Futility of futilities! All is futility."
verses.textEn: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Utterly meaningless! Everything is meaningless."

verses.textZh: 人的一切劳碌，就是他在日光之下的劳碌， 对自己有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 人的一切劳碌，就是他在日光之下的劳碌， 对自己有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 人一切的劳碌， 就是他在日光之下的劳碌，有什么益处呢？
verses.textEnNiv: What do people gain from all their labors at which they toil under the sun?
verses.textEnEsv: What does man gain by all the toil at which he toils under the sun?
verses.textEnNkjv: What profit has a man from all his labor In which he toils under the sun?
verses.textEnNlt: What do people get for all their hard work under the sun?
verses.textEnNasb: What advantage does a person have in all his work Which he does under the sun?
verses.textEn: What do people gain from all their labors at which they toil under the sun?

verses.textZh: 一代过去，一代又来， 地却永远存在。
verses.textZhCnvs: 一代过去，一代又来， 地却永远存在。
verses.textZhCuv: 一代过去，一代又来， 地却永远长存。
verses.textEnNiv: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
verses.textEnEsv: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth remains forever.
verses.textEnNkjv: One generation passes away, and another generation comes; But the earth abides forever.
verses.textEnNlt: Generations come and generations go, but the earth never changes.
verses.textEnNasb: A generation goes and a generation comes, But the earth remains forever.
verses.textEn: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

verses.textZh: 太阳升起，太阳落下， 匆忙回到它上升之处。
verses.textZhCnvs: 太阳升起，太阳落下， 匆忙回到它上升之处。
verses.textZhCuv: 日头出来，日头落下， 急归所出之地。
verses.textEnNiv: The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises.
verses.textEnEsv: The sun rises, and the sun goes down, and hastens to the place where it rises.
verses.textEnNkjv: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, And hastens to the place where it arose.
verses.textEnNlt: The sun rises and the sun sets, then hurries around to rise again.
verses.textEnNasb: Also, the sun rises and the sun sets; And hurrying to its place it rises there again.
verses.textEn: The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises.

verses.textZh: 风向南刮，又往北转， 循环周行，旋转不息。
verses.textZhCnvs: 风向南刮，又往北转， 循环周行，旋转不息。
verses.textZhCuv: 风往南刮，又向北转， 不住地旋转，而且返回转行原道。
verses.textEnNiv: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.
verses.textEnEsv: The wind blows to the south and goes around to the north; around and around goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.
verses.textEnNkjv: The wind goes toward the south, And turns around to the north; The wind whirls about continually, And comes again on its circuit.
verses.textEnNlt: The wind blows south, and then turns north. Around and around it goes, blowing in circles.
verses.textEnNasb: Blowing toward the south, Then turning toward the north, The wind continues swirling along; And on its circular courses the wind returns.
verses.textEn: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.

verses.textZh: 江河向海里流，海却不满溢； 江河之水归回本源，循环流转。
verses.textZhCnvs: 江河向海里流，海却不满溢； 江河之水归回本源，循环流转。
verses.textZhCuv: 江河都往海里流，海却不满； 江河从何处流，仍归还何处。
verses.textEnNiv: All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place the streams come from, there they return again.
verses.textEnEsv: All streams run to the sea, but the sea is not full; to the place where the streams flow, there they flow again.
verses.textEnNkjv: All the rivers run into the sea, Yet the sea is not full; To the place from which the rivers come, There they return again.
verses.textEnNlt: Rivers run into the sea, but the sea is never full. Then the water returns again to the rivers and flows out again to the sea.
verses.textEnNasb: All the rivers flow into the sea, Yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, There they flow again.
verses.textEn: All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place the streams come from, there they return again.

verses.textZh: 万事都令人厌倦， 人说，说不尽； 眼看，看不饱； 耳听，听不足。
verses.textZhCnvs: 万事都令人厌倦， 人说，说不尽； 眼看，看不饱； 耳听，听不足。
verses.textZhCuv: 万事令人厌烦 ， 人不能说尽。 眼看，看不饱； 耳听，听不足。
verses.textEnNiv: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.
verses.textEnEsv: All things are full of weariness; a man cannot utter it; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.textEnNkjv: All things are full of labor; Man cannot express it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.textEnNlt: Everything is wearisome beyond description. No matter how much we see, we are never satisfied. No matter how much we hear, we are not content.
verses.textEnNasb: All things are wearisome; No one can tell it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor is the ear filled with hearing.
verses.textEn: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.

verses.textZh: 已有的事必再有， 作过的事必再作； 日光之下并无新事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 已有的事必再有， 作过的事必再作； 日光之下并无新事。
verses.textZhCuv: 已有的事后必再有； 已行的事后必再行。 日光之下并无新事。
verses.textEnNiv: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done, and there is nothing new under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: That which has been is what will be, That which is done is what will be done, And thereis nothing new under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: History merely repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new.
verses.textEnNasb: What has been, it is what will be, And what has been done, it is what will be done. So there is nothing new under the sun.
verses.textEn: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

verses.textZh: 有甚么事人可以说： "看啊！这是新的"？ 其实，很久之前已经有了， 在我们之前早就有了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有甚么事人可以说： "看啊！这是新的"？ 其实，很久之前已经有了， 在我们之前早就有了。
verses.textZhCuv: 岂有一件事人能指着说这是新的？ 哪知，在我们以前的世代早已有了。
verses.textEnNiv: Is there anything of which one can say, "Look! This is something new"? It was here already, long ago; it was here before our time.
verses.textEnEsv: Is there a thing of which it is said, "See, this is new"? It has been already in the ages before us.
verses.textEnNkjv: Is there anything of which it may be said, "See, this is new"? It has already been in ancient times before us.
verses.textEnNlt: Sometimes people say, "Here is something new!" But actually it is old; nothing is ever truly new.
verses.textEnNasb: Is there anything of which one might say, "See this, it is new"? It has already existed for ages Which were before us.
verses.textEn: Is there anything of which one can say, "Look! This is something new"? It was here already, long ago; it was here before our time.

verses.textZh: 以前的事，无人记念； 将来的事，后来的人也不追忆。
verses.textZhCnvs: 以前的事，无人记念； 将来的事，后来的人也不追忆。
verses.textZhCuv: 已过的世代，无人记念； 将来的世代，后来的人也不记念。
verses.textEnNiv: No one remembers the former generations, and even those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow them.
verses.textEnEsv: There is no remembrance of former things, nor will there be any remembrance of later things yet to be among those who come after.
verses.textEnNkjv: Thereis no remembrance of former things, Nor will there be any remembrance of things that are to come By those who will come after.
verses.textEnNlt: We don’t remember what happened in the past, and in future generations, no one will remember what we are doing now.
verses.textEnNasb: There is no remembrance of the earlier things, And of the later things as well, which will occur, There will be no remembrance of them Among those who will come later still.
verses.textEn: No one remembers the former generations, and even those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow them.

verses.textZh: 那时，我传道者在耶路撒冷作以色列的王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那时，我传道者在耶路撒冷作以色列的王。
verses.textZhCuv: 我传道者在耶路撒冷作过以色列的王。
verses.textEnNiv: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnEsv: I the Preacher have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNlt: I, the Teacher, was king of Israel, and I lived in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: I, the Preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

verses.textZh: 我曾用智慧专心寻求查究天下所发生的一切事；原来神给予世人的，是劳苦的担子，叫他们为此烦恼。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我曾用智慧专心寻求查究天下所发生的一切事；原来神给予世人的，是劳苦的担子，叫他们为此烦恼。
verses.textZhCuv: 我专心用智慧寻求、查究天下所做的一切事，乃知神叫世人所经练的是极重的劳苦。
verses.textEnNiv: I applied my mind to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under the heavens. What a heavy burden God has laid on mankind!
verses.textEnEsv: And I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom all that is done under heaven. It is an unhappy business that God has given to the children of man to be busy with.
verses.textEnNkjv: And I set my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven; this burdensome task God has given to the sons of man, by which they may be exercised.
verses.textEnNlt: I devoted myself to search for understanding and to explore by wisdom everything being done under heaven. I soon discovered that God has dealt a tragic existence to the human race.
verses.textEnNasb: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom about everything that has been done under heaven. It is a sorry task with which God has given the sons of mankind to be troubled.
verses.textEn: I applied my mind to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under the heavens. What a heavy burden God has laid on mankind!

verses.textZh: 我看过日光之下所发生的一切事，不料，一切都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看过日光之下所发生的一切事，不料，一切都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下所做的一切事，都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: I have seen everything that is done under the sun, and behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and indeed, all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: I observed everything going on under the sun, and really, it is all meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen all the works which have been done under the sun, and behold, all is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 弯曲的，不能弄直；缺少的，不能数算。
verses.textZhCnvs: 弯曲的，不能弄直；缺少的，不能数算。
verses.textZhCuv: 弯曲的，不能变直； 缺少的，不能足数。
verses.textEnNiv: What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.
verses.textEnEsv: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
verses.textEnNkjv: Whatis crooked cannot be made straight, And what is lacking cannot be numbered.
verses.textEnNlt: What is wrong cannot be made right. What is missing cannot be recovered.
verses.textEnNasb: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
verses.textEn: What is crooked cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.

verses.textZh: 我自己心里说："我得了极大的智慧，胜过所有在我以前统治耶路撒冷的人；我见识了许多智慧与知识。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我自己心里说："我得了极大的智慧，胜过所有在我以前统治耶路撒冷的人；我见识了许多智慧与知识。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我心里议论说：我得了大智慧，胜过我以前在耶路撒冷的众人，而且我心中多经历智慧和知识的事。
verses.textEnNiv: I said to myself, "Look, I have increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge."
verses.textEnEsv: I said in my heart, "I have acquired great wisdom, surpassing all who were over Jerusalem before me, and my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge."
verses.textEnNkjv: I communed with my heart, saying, "Look, I have attained greatness, and have gained more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My heart has understood great wisdom and knowledge."
verses.textEnNlt: I said to myself, "Look, I am wiser than any of the kings who ruled in Jerusalem before me. I have greater wisdom and knowledge than any of them."
verses.textEnNasb: I said to myself, "Behold, I have magnified and increased wisdom more than all who were over Jerusalem before me; and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge."
verses.textEn: I said to myself, "Look, I have increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge."

verses.textZh: 我又专心究察智慧和知识，狂妄和愚昧，才知道这也是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我又专心究察智慧和知识，狂妄和愚昧，才知道这也是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又专心察明智慧、狂妄，和愚昧，乃知这也是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: And I applied my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is but a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: So I set out to learn everything from wisdom to madness and folly. But I learned firsthand that pursuing all this is like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: And I applied my mind to know wisdom and to know insanity and foolishness; I realized that this also is striving after wind.
verses.textEn: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 因为多有智慧，就多有烦恼；加增知识，就加增痛苦。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为多有智慧，就多有烦恼；加增知识，就加增痛苦。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为多有智慧，就多有愁烦； 加增知识的，就加增忧伤。
verses.textEnNiv: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.
verses.textEnEsv: For in much wisdom is much vexation, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
verses.textEnNkjv: For in much wisdom is much grief, And he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
verses.textEnNlt: The greater my wisdom, the greater my grief. To increase knowledge only increases sorrow.
verses.textEnNasb: Because in much wisdom there is much grief; and increasing knowledge results in increasing pain.
verses.textEn: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.

verses.textZh: 我自己心里说："来吧，我用享乐试试你，让你看看有甚么好处。"想不到，这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我自己心里说："来吧，我用享乐试试你，让你看看有甚么好处。"想不到，这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 我心里说：「来吧，我以喜乐试试你，你好享福！」谁知，这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: I said to myself, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good." But that also proved to be meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy yourself." But behold, this also was vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure"; but surely, this also was vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: I said to myself, "Come on, let’s try pleasure. Let’s look for the ‘good things’ in life." But I found that this, too, was meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: I said to myself, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure. So enjoy yourself." And behold, it too was futility.
verses.textEn: I said to myself, "Come now, I will test you with pleasure to find out what is good." But that also proved to be meaningless.

verses.textZh: 对嬉笑，我说："那是狂妄"；对享乐，我说："这有甚么作用呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 对嬉笑，我说："那是狂妄"；对享乐，我说："这有甚么作用呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 我指嬉笑说：「这是狂妄。」论喜乐说：「有何功效呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: "Laughter," I said, "is madness. And what does pleasure accomplish?"
verses.textEnEsv: I said of laughter, "It is mad," and of pleasure, "What use is it?"
verses.textEnNkjv: I said of laughter—"Madness!"; and of mirth, "What does it accomplish?"
verses.textEnNlt: So I said, "Laughter is silly. What good does it do to seek pleasure?"
verses.textEnNasb: I said of laughter, "It is senseless," and of pleasure, "What does this accomplish?"
verses.textEn: "Laughter," I said, "is madness. And what does pleasure accomplish?"

verses.textZh: 我心里筹思，怎样用酒使我的身体畅快，又保持愚昧，但我的内心仍由智慧引导；直到我看明世人，在诸天之下一生有限的年日中所行的，对他们有益的是甚么。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我心里筹思，怎样用酒使我的身体畅快，又保持愚昧，但我的内心仍由智慧引导；直到我看明世人，在诸天之下一生有限的年日中所行的，对他们有益的是甚么。
verses.textZhCuv: 我心里察究，如何用酒使我肉体舒畅，我心却仍以智慧引导我；又如何持住愚昧，等我看明世人，在天下一生当行何事为美。
verses.textEnNiv: I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was good for people to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.
verses.textEnEsv: I searched with my heart how to cheer my body with wine—my heart still guiding me with wisdom—and how to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was good for the children of man to do under heaven during the few days of their life.
verses.textEnNkjv: I searched in my heart how to gratify my flesh with wine, while guiding my heart with wisdom, and how to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was good for the sons of men to do under heaven all the days of their lives.
verses.textEnNlt: After much thought, I decided to cheer myself with wine. And while still seeking wisdom, I clutched at foolishness. In this way, I tried to experience the only happiness most people find during their brief life in this world.
verses.textEnNasb: I explored with my mind how to refresh my body with wine while my mind was guiding me wisely; and how to seize foolishness, until I could see what good there is for the sons of mankind to do under heaven for the few years of their lives.
verses.textEn: I tried cheering myself with wine, and embracing folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom. I wanted to see what was good for people to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.

verses.textZh: 我大事发展：为自己建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，
verses.textZhCnvs: 我大事发展：为自己建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，
verses.textZhCuv: 我为自己动大工程，建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，
verses.textEnNiv: I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.
verses.textEnEsv: I made great works. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.
verses.textEnNkjv: I made my works great, I built myself houses, and planted myself vineyards.
verses.textEnNlt: I also tried to find meaning by building huge homes for myself and by planting beautiful vineyards.
verses.textEnNasb: I enlarged my works: I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself;
verses.textEn: I undertook great projects: I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.

verses.textZh: 修造园囿和庭园，在园中栽种各类果树，
verses.textZhCnvs: 修造园囿和庭园，在园中栽种各类果树，
verses.textZhCuv: 修造园囿，在其中栽种各样果木树；
verses.textEnNiv: I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
verses.textEnEsv: I made myself gardens and parks, and planted in them all kinds of fruit trees.
verses.textEnNkjv: I made myself gardens and orchards, and I planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
verses.textEnNlt: I made gardens and parks, filling them with all kinds of fruit trees.
verses.textEnNasb: I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted in them all kinds of fruit trees;
verses.textEn: I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.

verses.textZh: 挖造水池，用来浇灌培植树木的林园。
verses.textZhCnvs: 挖造水池，用来浇灌培植树木的林园。
verses.textZhCuv: 挖造水池，用以浇灌嫩小的树木。
verses.textEnNiv: I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.
verses.textEnEsv: I made myself pools from which to water the forest of growing trees.
verses.textEnNkjv: I made myself water pools from which to water the growing trees of the grove.
verses.textEnNlt: I built reservoirs to collect the water to irrigate my many flourishing groves.
verses.textEnNasb: I made ponds of water for myself from which to irrigate a forest of growing trees.
verses.textEn: I made reservoirs to water groves of flourishing trees.

verses.textZh: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的奴仆；又拥有大群牛羊，胜过任何比我先在耶路撒冷的人所拥有的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的奴仆；又拥有大群牛羊，胜过任何比我先在耶路撒冷的人所拥有的。
verses.textZhCuv: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的仆婢；又有许多牛群羊群，胜过以前在耶路撒冷众人所有的。
verses.textEnNiv: I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
verses.textEnEsv: I bought male and female slaves, and had slaves who were born in my house. I had also great possessions of herds and flocks, more than any who had been before me in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: I acquired male and female servants, and had servants born in my house. Yes, I had greater possessions of herds and flocks than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
verses.textEnNlt: I bought slaves, both men and women, and others were born into my household. I also owned large herds and flocks, more than any of the kings who had lived in Jerusalem before me.
verses.textEnNasb: I bought male and female slaves, and I had slaves born at home. I also possessed flocks and herds larger than all who preceded me in Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: I bought male and female slaves and had other slaves who were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.

verses.textZh: 我又为自己积蓄金银，以及列王和各省的财宝。我又为自己招募男女歌手，收纳许多妃嫔，是世人所以为乐的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我又为自己积蓄金银，以及列王和各省的财宝。我又为自己招募男女歌手，收纳许多妃嫔，是世人所以为乐的。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又为自己积蓄金银和君王的财宝，并各省的财宝；又得唱歌的男女和世人所喜爱的物，并许多的妃嫔。
verses.textEnNiv: I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem as well—the delights of a man’s heart.
verses.textEnEsv: I also gathered for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got singers, both men and women, and many concubines, the delight of the sons of man.
verses.textEnNkjv: I also gathered for myself silver and gold and the special treasures of kings and of the provinces. I acquired male and female singers, the delights of the sons of men, and musical instruments of all kinds.
verses.textEnNlt: I collected great sums of silver and gold, the treasure of many kings and provinces. I hired wonderful singers, both men and women, and had many beautiful concubines. I had everything a man could desire!
verses.textEnNasb: I also amassed for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I provided for myself male and female singers, and the pleasures of the sons of mankind: many concubines.
verses.textEn: I amassed silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I acquired male and female singers, and a harem as well—the delights of a man’s heart.

verses.textZh: 于是我就日渐昌大，超过任何比我先在耶路撒冷的人；我的智慧仍然与我同在。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我就日渐昌大，超过任何比我先在耶路撒冷的人；我的智慧仍然与我同在。
verses.textZhCuv: 这样，我就日见昌盛，胜过以前在耶路撒冷的众人。我的智慧仍然存留。
verses.textEnNiv: I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.
verses.textEnEsv: So I became great and surpassed all who were before me in Jerusalem. Also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.textEnNkjv: So I became great and excelled more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. Also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.textEnNlt: So I became greater than all who had lived in Jerusalem before me, and my wisdom never failed me.
verses.textEnNasb: Then I became great and increased more than all who preceded me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also stood by me.
verses.textEn: I became greater by far than anyone in Jerusalem before me. In all this my wisdom stayed with me.

verses.textZh: 我眼中所求的，我都不禁止；我心所喜欢的，我都没抑制。我的心因我的一切劳碌而快乐，这就是我从一切劳碌中所得的分。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我眼中所求的，我都不禁止；我心所喜欢的，我都没抑制。我的心因我的一切劳碌而快乐，这就是我从一切劳碌中所得的分。
verses.textZhCuv: 凡我眼所求的，我没有留下不给它的；我心所乐的，我没有禁止不享受的；因我的心为我一切所劳碌的快乐，这就是我从劳碌中所得的分。
verses.textEnNiv: I denied myself nothing my eyes desired; I refused my heart no pleasure. My heart took delight in all my labor, and this was the reward for all my toil.
verses.textEnEsv: And whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them. I kept my heart from no pleasure, for my heart found pleasure in all my toil, and this was my reward for all my toil.
verses.textEnNkjv: Whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them. I did not withhold my heart from any pleasure, For my heart rejoiced in all my labor; And this was my reward from all my labor.
verses.textEnNlt: Anything I wanted, I would take. I denied myself no pleasure. I even found great pleasure in hard work, a reward for all my labors.
verses.textEnNasb: All that my eyes desired, I did not refuse them. I did not restrain my heart from any pleasure, for my heart was pleased because of all my labor; and this was my reward for all my labor.
verses.textEn: I denied myself nothing my eyes desired; I refused my heart no pleasure. My heart took delight in all my labor, and this was the reward for all my toil.

verses.textZh: 然后，我省察我手所作的一切，和我劳碌所成就的，想不到一切都是虚空，都是捕风，在日光之下毫无益处。
verses.textZhCnvs: 然后，我省察我手所作的一切，和我劳碌所成就的，想不到一切都是虚空，都是捕风，在日光之下毫无益处。
verses.textZhCuv: 后来，我察看我手所经营的一切事和我劳碌所成的功。谁知都是虚空，都是捕风；在日光之下毫无益处。
verses.textEnNiv: Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done and what I had toiled to achieve, everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind; nothing was gained under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: Then I considered all that my hands had done and the toil I had expended in doing it, and behold, all was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had done And on the labor in which I had toiled; And indeed all was vanity and grasping for the wind. Therewas no profit under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: But as I looked at everything I had worked so hard to accomplish, it was all so meaningless—like chasing the wind. There was nothing really worthwhile anywhere.
verses.textEnNasb: So I considered all my activities which my hands had done and the labor which I had exerted, and behold, all was futility and striving after wind, and there was no benefit under the sun.
verses.textEn: Yet when I surveyed all that my hands had done and what I had toiled to achieve, everything was meaningless, a chasing after the wind; nothing was gained under the sun.

verses.textZh: 我转过来观察智慧、狂妄和愚昧。王的继承人还能作甚么呢？只不过作先前作过的罢了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我转过来观察智慧、狂妄和愚昧。王的继承人还能作甚么呢？只不过作先前作过的罢了。
verses.textZhCuv: 我转念观看智慧、狂妄，和愚昧。在王以后而来的人还能做什么呢？也不过行早先所行的就是了。
verses.textEnNiv: Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom, and also madness and folly. What more can the king’s successor do than what has already been done?
verses.textEnEsv: So I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly. For what can the man do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I turned myself to consider wisdom and madness and folly; For what can the man do who succeeds the king?— Only what he has already done.
verses.textEnNlt: So I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and madness (for who can do this better than I, the king? ).
verses.textEnNasb: So I turned to consider wisdom, insanity, and foolishness; for what will the man do who will come after the king, except what has already been done?
verses.textEn: Then I turned my thoughts to consider wisdom, and also madness and folly. What more can the king’s successor do than what has already been done?

verses.textZh: 于是我看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗一样。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗一样。
verses.textZhCuv: 我便看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗。
verses.textEnNiv: I saw that wisdom is better than folly, just as light is better than darkness.
verses.textEnEsv: Then I saw that there is more gain in wisdom than in folly, as there is more gain in light than in darkness.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly As light excels darkness.
verses.textEnNlt: I thought, "Wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
verses.textEnNasb: Then I saw that wisdom surpasses foolishness as light surpasses darkness.
verses.textEn: I saw that wisdom is better than folly, just as light is better than darkness.

verses.textZh: 智慧人的眼目明亮，愚昧人却走在黑暗中。我也知道同一的命运要临到这两种人身上。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人的眼目明亮，愚昧人却走在黑暗中。我也知道同一的命运要临到这两种人身上。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人的眼目光明 ，愚昧人在黑暗里行。我却看明有一件事，这两等人都必遇见。
verses.textEnNiv: The wise have eyes in their heads, while the fool walks in the darkness; but I came to realize that the same fate overtakes them both.
verses.textEnEsv: The wise person has his eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. And yet I perceived that the same event happens to all of them.
verses.textEnNkjv: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, But the fool walks in darkness. Yet I myself perceived That the same event happens to them all.
verses.textEnNlt: For the wise can see where they are going, but fools walk in the dark." Yet I saw that the wise and the foolish share the same fate.
verses.textEnNasb: The wise person’s eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. And yet I know that one and the same fate happens to both of them.
verses.textEn: The wise have eyes in their heads, while the fool walks in the darkness; but I came to realize that the same fate overtakes them both.

verses.textZh: 我自己心里说："临到愚昧人身上的，也必临到我身上；那么，我为甚么要更有智慧呢？"于是我心里说："这也是虚空。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我自己心里说："临到愚昧人身上的，也必临到我身上；那么，我为甚么要更有智慧呢？"于是我心里说："这也是虚空。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我就心里说：「愚昧人所遇见的，我也必遇见，我为何更有智慧呢？」我心里说，这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: Then I said to myself, "The fate of the fool will overtake me also. What then do I gain by being wise?" I said to myself, "This too is meaningless."
verses.textEnEsv: Then I said in my heart, "What happens to the fool will happen to me also. Why then have I been so very wise?" And I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: So I said in my heart, "As it happens to the fool, It also happens to me, And why was I then more wise?" Then I said in my heart, "This also is vanity."
verses.textEnNlt: Both will die. So I said to myself, "Since I will end up the same as the fool, what’s the value of all my wisdom? This is all so meaningless!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then I said to myself, "As is the fate of the fool, it will also happen to me. Why then have I been extremely wise?" So I said to myself, "This too is futility."
verses.textEn: Then I said to myself, "The fate of the fool will overtake me also. What then do I gain by being wise?" I said to myself, "This too is meaningless."

verses.textZh: 因为智慧人和愚昧人一样，没有人永远记念他们，在未来的日子里，都会被人遗忘。可叹智慧人跟愚昧人一样，终必死亡。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为智慧人和愚昧人一样，没有人永远记念他们，在未来的日子里，都会被人遗忘。可叹智慧人跟愚昧人一样，终必死亡。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人和愚昧人一样，永远无人记念，因为日后都被忘记；可叹智慧人死亡，与愚昧人无异。
verses.textEnNiv: For the wise, like the fool, will not be long remembered; the days have already come when both have been forgotten. Like the fool, the wise too must die!
verses.textEnEsv: For of the wise as of the fool there is no enduring remembrance, seeing that in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. How the wise dies just like the fool!
verses.textEnNkjv: For thereis no more remembrance of the wise than of the fool forever, Since all that now is will be forgotten in the days to come. And how does a wise man die? As the fool!
verses.textEnNlt: For the wise and the foolish both die. The wise will not be remembered any longer than the fool. In the days to come, both will be forgotten.
verses.textEnNasb: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, along with the fool, since in the coming days everything will soon be forgotten. And how the wise and the fool alike die!
verses.textEn: For the wise, like the fool, will not be long remembered; the days have already come when both have been forgotten. Like the fool, the wise too must die!

verses.textZh: 因此我恨恶生命，因为在日光之下所发生的事，都使我厌烦。一切都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因此我恨恶生命，因为在日光之下所发生的事，都使我厌烦。一切都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 我所以恨恶生命；因为在日光之下所行的事我都以为烦恼，都是虚空，都是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: So I hated life, because what is done under the sun was grievous to me, for all is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore I hated life because the work that was done under the sun was distressing to me, for all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: So I came to hate life because everything done here under the sun is so troubling. Everything is meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: So I hated life, for the work which had been done under the sun was unhappy to me; because everything is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. All of it is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 我恨恶我的一切劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌，因为我不得不把劳碌的成果留给后人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我恨恶我的一切劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌，因为我不得不把劳碌的成果留给后人。
verses.textZhCuv: 我恨恶一切的劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌，因为我得来的必留给我以后的人。
verses.textEnNiv: I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.
verses.textEnEsv: I hated all my toil in which I toil under the sun, seeing that I must leave it to the man who will come after me,
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I hated all my labor in which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.
verses.textEnNlt: I came to hate all my hard work here on earth, for I must leave to others everything I have earned.
verses.textEnNasb: So I hated all the fruit of my labor for which I had labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.
verses.textEn: I hated all the things I had toiled for under the sun, because I must leave them to the one who comes after me.

verses.textZh: 那人将来是智是愚，有谁晓得呢？可是他竟要掌管一切我劳碌得来的，就是我在日光之下用智慧得来的。这又是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那人将来是智是愚，有谁晓得呢？可是他竟要掌管一切我劳碌得来的，就是我在日光之下用智慧得来的。这又是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 那人是智慧是愚昧，谁能知道？他竟要管理我劳碌所得的，就是我在日光之下用智慧所得的。这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will have control over all the fruit of my toil into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: and who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will be master of all for which I toiled and used my wisdom under the sun. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will rule over all my labor in which I toiled and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: And who can tell whether my successors will be wise or foolish? Yet they will control everything I have gained by my skill and hard work under the sun. How meaningless!
verses.textEnNasb: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will have control over all the fruit of my labor for which I have labored by acting wisely under the sun. This too is futility.
verses.textEn: And who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? Yet they will have control over all the fruit of my toil into which I have poured my effort and skill under the sun. This too is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 于是我转念，对日光之下我所劳碌的一切，心感绝望；
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我转念，对日光之下我所劳碌的一切，心感绝望；
verses.textZhCuv: 故此，我转想我在日光之下所劳碌的一切工作，心便绝望。
verses.textEnNiv: So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labor under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: So I turned about and gave my heart up to despair over all the toil of my labors under the sun,
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore I turned my heart and despaired of all the labor in which I had toiled under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: So I gave up in despair, questioning the value of all my hard work in this world.
verses.textEnNasb: Therefore I completely despaired over all the fruit of my labor for which I had labored under the sun.
verses.textEn: So my heart began to despair over all my toilsome labor under the sun.

verses.textZh: 因为人用智慧、知识和技能所劳碌得来的，却必须留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，是极大的憾事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为人用智慧、知识和技能所劳碌得来的，却必须留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，是极大的憾事。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为有人用智慧、知识、灵巧所劳碌得来的，却要留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，也是大患。
verses.textEnNiv: For a person may labor with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.
verses.textEnEsv: because sometimes a person who has toiled with wisdom and knowledge and skill must leave everything to be enjoyed by someone who did not toil for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.textEnNkjv: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill; yet he must leave his heritage to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
verses.textEnNlt: Some people work wisely with knowledge and skill, then must leave the fruit of their efforts to someone who hasn’t worked for it. This, too, is meaningless, a great tragedy.
verses.textEnNasb: When there is a person who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and then gives his legacy to one who has not labored for it; this too is futility and a great evil.
verses.textEn: For a person may labor with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then they must leave all they own to another who has not toiled for it. This too is meaningless and a great misfortune.

verses.textZh: 人的一切劳碌和操心，就是他在日光之下所劳碌的，对自己有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 人的一切劳碌和操心，就是他在日光之下所劳碌的，对自己有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 人在日光之下劳碌累心，在他一切的劳碌上得着什么呢？
verses.textEnNiv: What do people get for all the toil and anxious striving with which they labor under the sun?
verses.textEnEsv: What has a man from all the toil and striving of heart with which he toils beneath the sun?
verses.textEnNkjv: For what has man for all his labor, and for the striving of his heart with which he has toiled under the sun?
verses.textEnNlt: So what do people get in this life for all their hard work and anxiety?
verses.textEnNasb: For what does a person get in all his labor and in his striving with which he labors under the sun?
verses.textEn: What do people get for all the toil and anxious striving with which they labor under the sun?

verses.textZh: 其实终其一生，他的担子既痛苦又烦恼，在夜间也不能安心。这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 其实终其一生，他的担子既痛苦又烦恼，在夜间也不能安心。这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为他日日忧虑，他的劳苦成为愁烦，连夜间心也不安。这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: All their days their work is grief and pain; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: For all his days are full of sorrow, and his work is a vexation. Even in the night his heart does not rest. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: For all his days are sorrowful, and his work burdensome; even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: Their days of labor are filled with pain and grief; even at night their minds cannot rest. It is all meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: Because all his days his activity is painful and irritating; even at night his mind does not rest. This too is futility.
verses.textEn: All their days their work is grief and pain; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 人最好是吃喝，在自己的劳碌中自得其乐；我看这也是出于神的手。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人最好是吃喝，在自己的劳碌中自得其乐；我看这也是出于神的手。
verses.textZhCuv: 人莫强如吃喝，且在劳碌中享福，我看这也是出于神的手。
verses.textEnNiv: A person can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their own toil. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,
verses.textEnEsv: There is nothing better for a person than that he should eat and drink and find enjoyment in his toil. This also, I saw, is from the hand of God,
verses.textEnNkjv: Nothing is better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and that his soul should enjoy good in his labor. This also, I saw, was from the hand of God.
verses.textEnNlt: So I decided there is nothing better than to enjoy food and drink and to find satisfaction in work. Then I realized that these pleasures are from the hand of God.
verses.textEnNasb: There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink, and show himself some good in his trouble. This too I have seen, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.textEn: A person can do nothing better than to eat and drink and find satisfaction in their own toil. This too, I see, is from the hand of God,

verses.textZh: 离开了他 ，谁能有吃的呢？谁能享乐呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 离开了他 ，谁能有吃的呢？谁能享乐呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 论到吃用、享福，谁能胜过我呢？
verses.textEnNiv: for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?
verses.textEnEsv: for apart from him who can eat or who can have enjoyment?
verses.textEnNkjv: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
verses.textEnNlt: For who can eat or enjoy anything apart from him?
verses.textEnNasb: For who can eat and who can have enjoyment without Him?
verses.textEn: for without him, who can eat or find enjoyment?

verses.textZh: 神把智慧、知识和喜乐赐给他所喜悦的人，却使罪人作收集和积聚的差事，把所得的归给神所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 神把智慧、知识和喜乐赐给他所喜悦的人，却使罪人作收集和积聚的差事，把所得的归给神所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 神喜悦谁，就给谁智慧、知识，和喜乐；惟有罪人，神使他劳苦，叫他将所收聚的、所堆积的归给神所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: For to the one who pleases him God has given wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner he has given the business of gathering and collecting, only to give to one who pleases God. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: For God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy to a man who is good in His sight; but to the sinner He gives the work of gathering and collecting, that he may give to himwhois good before God. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to those who please him. But if a sinner becomes wealthy, God takes the wealth away and gives it to those who please him. This, too, is meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: For to a person who is good in His sight, He has given wisdom and knowledge and joy, while to the sinner He has given the task of gathering and collecting so that he may give to one who is good in God’s sight. This too is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: To the person who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge and happiness, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and storing up wealth to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 万事都有定期，天下万务都有定时：
verses.textZhCnvs: 万事都有定期，天下万务都有定时：
verses.textZhCuv: 凡事都有定期， 天下万务都有定时。
verses.textEnNiv: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens:
verses.textEnEsv: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven:
verses.textEnNkjv: To everything thereis a season, A time for every purpose under heaven:
verses.textEnNlt: For everything there is a season, a time for every activity under heaven.
verses.textEnNasb: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every matter under heaven—
verses.textEn: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens:

verses.textZh: 生有时，死有时； 栽种有时，拔出所种的也有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 生有时，死有时； 栽种有时，拔出所种的也有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 生有时，死有时； 栽种有时，拔出所栽种的也有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what is planted;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to be born, And a time to die; A time to plant, And a time to pluck whatis planted;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to be born and a time to die. A time to plant and a time to harvest.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to give birth and a time to die; A time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted.
verses.textEn: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,

verses.textZh: 杀戮有时，医治有时； 拆毁有时，建造有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 杀戮有时，医治有时； 拆毁有时，建造有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 杀戮有时，医治有时； 拆毁有时，建造有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to kill, And a time to heal; A time to break down, And a time to build up;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to kill and a time to heal. A time to tear down and a time to build up.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to kill and a time to heal; A time to tear down and a time to build up.
verses.textEn: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build,

verses.textZh: 哭有时，笑有时； 哀恸有时，踊跃有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 哭有时，笑有时； 哀恸有时，踊跃有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 哭有时，笑有时； 哀恸有时，跳舞有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to weep, And a time to laugh; A time to mourn, And a time to dance;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to cry and a time to laugh. A time to grieve and a time to dance.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to weep and a time to laugh; A time to mourn and a time to dance.
verses.textEn: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,

verses.textZh: 拋掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时； 拥抱有时，避免拥抱有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 拋掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时； 拥抱有时，避免拥抱有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 抛掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时； 怀抱有时，不怀抱有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to cast away stones, And a time to gather stones; A time to embrace, And a time to refrain from embracing;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to scatter stones and a time to gather stones. A time to embrace and a time to turn away.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; A time to embrace and a time to shun embracing.
verses.textEn: a time to scatter stones and a time to gather them, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,

verses.textZh: 寻找有时，舍弃有时； 保存有时，拋弃有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 寻找有时，舍弃有时； 保存有时，拋弃有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 寻找有时，失落有时； 保守有时，舍弃有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to search and a time to give up, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to gain, And a time to lose; A time to keep, And a time to throw away;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to search and a time to quit searching. A time to keep and a time to throw away.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to search and a time to give up as lost; A time to keep and a time to throw away.
verses.textEn: a time to search and a time to give up, a time to keep and a time to throw away,

verses.textZh: 撕裂有时，缝补有时； 静默有时，讲话有时；
verses.textZhCnvs: 撕裂有时，缝补有时； 静默有时，讲话有时；
verses.textZhCuv: 撕裂有时，缝补有时； 静默有时，言语有时；
verses.textEnNiv: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
verses.textEnEsv: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to tear, And a time to sew; A time to keep silence, And a time to speak;
verses.textEnNlt: A time to tear and a time to mend. A time to be quiet and a time to speak.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to tear apart and a time to sew together; A time to be silent and a time to speak.
verses.textEn: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,

verses.textZh: 爱有时，恨有时； 战争有时，和平有时。
verses.textZhCnvs: 爱有时，恨有时； 战争有时，和平有时。
verses.textZhCuv: 喜爱有时，恨恶有时； 争战有时，和好有时。
verses.textEnNiv: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
verses.textEnEsv: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
verses.textEnNkjv: A time to love, And a time to hate; A time of war, And a time of peace.
verses.textEnNlt: A time to love and a time to hate. A time for war and a time for peace.
verses.textEnNasb: A time to love and a time to hate; A time for war and a time for peace.
verses.textEn: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.

verses.textZh: 作工的人在自己的劳碌上得到甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 作工的人在自己的劳碌上得到甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 这样看来，做事的人在他的劳碌上有什么益处呢？
verses.textEnNiv: What do workers gain from their toil?
verses.textEnEsv: What gain has the worker from his toil?
verses.textEnNkjv: What profit has the worker from that in which he labors?
verses.textEnNlt: What do people really get for all their hard work?
verses.textEnNasb: What benefit is there for the worker from that in which he labors?
verses.textEn: What do workers gain from their toil?

verses.textZh: 我看神给予世人的担子，是要他们为此烦恼。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看神给予世人的担子，是要他们为此烦恼。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见神叫世人劳苦，使他们在其中受经练。
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.
verses.textEnEsv: I have seen the business that God has given to the children of man to be busy with.
verses.textEnNkjv: I have seen the God-given task with which the sons of men are to be occupied.
verses.textEnNlt: I have seen the burden God has placed on us all.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen the task which God has given the sons of mankind with which to occupy themselves.
verses.textEn: I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.

verses.textZh: 他使万事各按其时，成为美好；他又把永恒的意识放在人的心里；虽然这样，人还是不能察觉神自始至终的作为。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他使万事各按其时，成为美好；他又把永恒的意识放在人的心里；虽然这样，人还是不能察觉神自始至终的作为。
verses.textZhCuv: 神造万物，各按其时成为美好，又将永生 安置在世人心里。然而神从始至终的作为，人不能参透。
verses.textEnNiv: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
verses.textEnEsv: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also, he has put eternity into man’s heart, yet so that he cannot find out what God has done from the beginning to the end.
verses.textEnNkjv: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also He has put eternity in their hearts, except that no one can find out the work that God does from beginning to end.
verses.textEnNlt: Yet God has made everything beautiful for its own time. He has planted eternity in the human heart, but even so, people cannot see the whole scope of God’s work from beginning to end.
verses.textEnNasb: He has made everything appropriate in its time. He has also set eternity in their heart, without the possibility that mankind will find out the work which God has done from the beginning even to the end.
verses.textEn: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end.

verses.textZh: 我晓得人生最好是寻乐享福，
verses.textZhCnvs: 我晓得人生最好是寻乐享福，
verses.textZhCuv: 我知道世人，莫强如终身喜乐行善；
verses.textEnNiv: I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live.
verses.textEnEsv: I perceived that there is nothing better for them than to be joyful and to do good as long as they live;
verses.textEnNkjv: I know that nothing is better for them than to rejoice, and to do good in their lives,
verses.textEnNlt: So I concluded there is nothing better than to be happy and enjoy ourselves as long as we can.
verses.textEnNasb: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in one’s lifetime;
verses.textEn: I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live.

verses.textZh: 人人有吃有喝，在自己的一切劳碌中自得其乐；这就是神的恩赐。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人人有吃有喝，在自己的一切劳碌中自得其乐；这就是神的恩赐。
verses.textZhCuv: 并且人人吃喝，在他一切劳碌中享福，这也是神的恩赐。
verses.textEnNiv: That each of them may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil—this is the gift of God.
verses.textEnEsv: also that everyone should eat and drink and take pleasure in all his toil—this is God’s gift to man.
verses.textEnNkjv: and also that every man should eat and drink and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
verses.textEnNlt: And people should eat and drink and enjoy the fruits of their labor, for these are gifts from God.
verses.textEnNasb: moreover, that every person who eats and drinks sees good in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
verses.textEn: That each of them may eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil—this is the gift of God.

verses.textZh: 我知道神所作的一切，都必永存，无可增添，无可减少；神这样作，为要使人在他面前存敬畏的心。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我知道神所作的一切，都必永存，无可增添，无可减少；神这样作，为要使人在他面前存敬畏的心。
verses.textZhCuv: 我知道神一切所做的都必永存；无所增添，无所减少。神这样行，是要人在他面前存敬畏的心。
verses.textEnNiv: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that people will fear him.
verses.textEnEsv: I perceived that whatever God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it. God has done it, so that people fear before him.
verses.textEnNkjv: I know that whatever God does, It shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, And nothing taken from it. God does it, that men should fear before Him.
verses.textEnNlt: And I know that whatever God does is final. Nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God’s purpose is that people should fear him.
verses.textEnNasb: I know that everything God does will remain forever; there is nothing to add to it and there is nothing to take from it. And God has so worked, that people will fear Him.
verses.textEn: I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does it so that people will fear him.

verses.textZh: 现在有的，先前就有；将来有的，早已有了；因为神使已过的事重新出现 。
verses.textZhCnvs: 现在有的，先前就有；将来有的，早已有了；因为神使已过的事重新出现 。
verses.textZhCuv: 现今的事早先就有了，将来的事早已也有了，并且神使已过的事重新再来 。
verses.textEnNiv: Whatever is has already been, and what will be has been before; and God will call the past to account.
verses.textEnEsv: That which is, already has been; that which is to be, already has been; and God seeks what has been driven away.
verses.textEnNkjv: That which is has already been, And what is to be has already been; And God requires an account of what is past.
verses.textEnNlt: What is happening now has happened before, and what will happen in the future has happened before, because God makes the same things happen over and over again.
verses.textEnNasb: That which is, is what has already been, and that which will be has already been; and God seeks what has passed by.
verses.textEn: Whatever is has already been, and what will be has been before; and God will call the past to account.

verses.textZh: 我在日光之下又看见：审判的地方有奸恶，维护公义的地方也有奸恶。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我在日光之下又看见：审判的地方有奸恶，维护公义的地方也有奸恶。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又见日光之下，在审判之处有奸恶，在公义之处也有奸恶。
verses.textEnNiv: And I saw something else under the sun: In the place of judgment—wickedness was there, in the place of justice—wickedness was there.
verses.textEnEsv: Moreover, I saw under the sun that in the place of justice, even there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness, even there was wickedness.
verses.textEnNkjv: Moreover I saw under the sun: In the place of judgment, Wickedness was there; And in the place of righteousness, Iniquity was there.
verses.textEnNlt: I also noticed that under the sun there is evil in the courtroom. Yes, even the courts of law are corrupt!
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, I have seen under the sun that in the place of justice there is wickedness and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
verses.textEn: And I saw something else under the sun: In the place of judgment—wickedness was there, in the place of justice—wickedness was there.

verses.textZh: 我自己心里说："神必审判义人和恶人，因为各样事务、各样工作都有定时。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我自己心里说："神必审判义人和恶人，因为各样事务、各样工作都有定时。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我心里说，神必审判义人和恶人；因为在那里，各样事务，一切工作，都有定时。
verses.textEnNiv: I said to myself, "God will bring into judgment both the righteous and the wicked, for there will be a time for every activity, a time to judge every deed."
verses.textEnEsv: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and for every work.
verses.textEnNkjv: I said in my heart, "God shall judge the righteous and the wicked, For thereis a time there for every purpose and for every work."
verses.textEnNlt: I said to myself, "In due season God will judge everyone, both good and bad, for all their deeds."
verses.textEnNasb: I said to myself, "God will judge the righteous and the wicked," for a time for every matter and for every deed is there.
verses.textEn: I said to myself, "God will bring into judgment both the righteous and the wicked, for there will be a time for every activity, a time to judge every deed."

verses.textZh: 我自己心里说："至于世人，神要试验他们，使他们看见自己与牲畜无异。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我自己心里说："至于世人，神要试验他们，使他们看见自己与牲畜无异。
verses.textZhCuv: 我心里说，这乃为世人的缘故，是神要试验他们，使他们觉得自己不过像兽一样。
verses.textEnNiv: I also said to myself, "As for humans, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.
verses.textEnEsv: I said in my heart with regard to the children of man that God is testing them that they may see that they themselves are but beasts.
verses.textEnNkjv: I said in my heart, "Concerning the condition of the sons of men, God tests them, that they may see that they themselves are like animals."
verses.textEnNlt: I also thought about the human condition—how God proves to people that they are like animals.
verses.textEnNasb: I said to myself regarding the sons of mankind, "God is testing them in order for them to see that they are as animals, they to themselves."
verses.textEn: I also said to myself, "As for humans, God tests them so that they may see that they are like the animals.

verses.textZh: 因为世人所遭遇的与牲畜所遭遇的，都是一样：这个怎样死，那个也怎样死，两者的气息都是一样，所以人并不胜于牲畜。一切都是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为世人所遭遇的与牲畜所遭遇的，都是一样：这个怎样死，那个也怎样死，两者的气息都是一样，所以人并不胜于牲畜。一切都是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为世人遭遇的，兽也遭遇，所遭遇的都是一样：这个怎样死，那个也怎样死，气息都是一样。人不能强于兽，都是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: Surely the fate of human beings is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath ; humans have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: For what happens to the children of man and what happens to the beasts is the same; as one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath, and man has no advantage over the beasts, for all is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: For what happens to the sons of men also happens to animals; one thing befalls them: as one dies, so dies the other. Surely, they all have one breath; man has no advantage over animals, for all is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: For people and animals share the same fate—both breathe and both must die. So people have no real advantage over the animals. How meaningless!
verses.textEnNasb: For the fate of the sons of mankind and the fate of animals is the same. As one dies, so dies the other; indeed, they all have the same breath, and there is no advantage for mankind over animals, for all is futility.
verses.textEn: Surely the fate of human beings is like that of the animals; the same fate awaits them both: As one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath ; humans have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 大家都到一个地方去，都出于尘土，也都归回尘土。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大家都到一个地方去，都出于尘土，也都归回尘土。
verses.textZhCuv: 都归一处，都是出于尘土，也都归于尘土。
verses.textEnNiv: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.
verses.textEnEsv: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and to dust all return.
verses.textEnNkjv: All go to one place: all are from the dust, and all return to dust.
verses.textEnNlt: Both go to the same place—they came from dust and they return to dust.
verses.textEnNasb: All go to the same place. All came from the dust and all return to the dust.
verses.textEn: All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.

verses.textZh: 有谁知道人的灵是往上升，牲畜的魂 是下降而入地呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 有谁知道人的灵是往上升，牲畜的魂 是下降而入地呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 谁知道人的灵是往上升，兽的魂是下入地呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Who knows if the human spirit rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?"
verses.textEnEsv: Who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward and the spirit of the beast goes down into the earth?
verses.textEnNkjv: Who knows the spirit of the sons of men, which goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, which goes down to the earth?
verses.textEnNlt: For who can prove that the human spirit goes up and the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?
verses.textEnNasb: Who knows that the spirit of the sons of mankind ascends upward and the spirit of the animal descends downward to the earth?
verses.textEn: Who knows if the human spirit rises upward and if the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?"

verses.textZh: 因此我看人最好是在自己所作的事上自得其乐，因为这也是他的分；谁能使他看见他自己死后的事呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 因此我看人最好是在自己所作的事上自得其乐，因为这也是他的分；谁能使他看见他自己死后的事呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 故此，我见人莫强如在他经营的事上喜乐，因为这是他的分。他身后的事谁能使他回来得见呢？
verses.textEnNiv: So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy their work, because that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?
verses.textEnEsv: So I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his work, for that is his lot. Who can bring him to see what will be after him?
verses.textEnNkjv: So I perceived that nothing is better than that a man should rejoice in his own works, for that is his heritage. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?
verses.textEnNlt: So I saw that there is nothing better for people than to be happy in their work. That is our lot in life. And no one can bring us back to see what happens after we die.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen that nothing is better than when a person is happy in his activities, for that is his lot. For who will bring him to see what will occur after him?
verses.textEn: So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to enjoy their work, because that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?

verses.textZh: 我又看见日光之下所发生一切欺压的事：受欺压的流泪，却无人安慰他们；欺压他们的，手里握着权柄，因此无人安慰受欺压的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我又看见日光之下所发生一切欺压的事：受欺压的流泪，却无人安慰他们；欺压他们的，手里握着权柄，因此无人安慰受欺压的。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又转念，见日光之下所行的一切欺压。看哪，受欺压的流泪，且无人安慰；欺压他们的有势力，也无人安慰他们。
verses.textEnNiv: Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun: I saw the tears of the oppressed— and they have no comforter; power was on the side of their oppressors— and they have no comforter.
verses.textEnEsv: Again I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they had no one to comfort them! On the side of their oppressors there was power, and there was no one to comfort them.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I returned and considered all the oppression that is done under the sun: And look! The tears of the oppressed, But they have no comforter— On the side of their oppressors thereis power, But they have no comforter.
verses.textEnNlt: Again, I observed all the oppression that takes place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, with no one to comfort them. The oppressors have great power, and their victims are helpless.
verses.textEnNasb: Then I looked again at all the acts of oppression which were being done under the sun. And behold, I saw the tears of the oppressed and that they had no one to comfort them; and power was on the side of their oppressors, but they had no one to comfort them.
verses.textEn: Again I looked and saw all the oppression that was taking place under the sun: I saw the tears of the oppressed— and they have no comforter; power was on the side of their oppressors— and they have no comforter.

verses.textZh: 我赞叹那已死的人，胜过那还活着的人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我赞叹那已死的人，胜过那还活着的人。
verses.textZhCuv: 因此，我赞叹那早已死的死人，胜过那还活着的活人。
verses.textEnNiv: And I declared that the dead, who had already died, are happier than the living, who are still alive.
verses.textEnEsv: And I thought the dead who are already dead more fortunate than the living who are still alive.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore I praised the dead who were already dead, More than the living who are still alive.
verses.textEnNlt: So I concluded that the dead are better off than the living.
verses.textEnNasb: So I congratulated the dead who are already dead, more than the living who are still living.
verses.textEn: And I declared that the dead, who had already died, are happier than the living, who are still alive.

verses.textZh: 那还没生下来的，就是还没看过日光之下所行的恶事的，比这两种人更有福。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那还没生下来的，就是还没看过日光之下所行的恶事的，比这两种人更有福。
verses.textZhCuv: 并且我以为那未曾生的，就是未见过日光之下恶事的，比这两等人更强。
verses.textEnNiv: But better than both is the one who has never been born, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: But better than both is he who has not yet been and has not seen the evil deeds that are done under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Yet, better than both ishe who has never existed, Who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: But most fortunate of all are those who are not yet born. For they have not seen all the evil that is done under the sun.
verses.textEnNasb: But better off than both of them is the one who has never existed, who has never seen the evil activity that is done under the sun.
verses.textEn: But better than both is the one who has never been born, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.

verses.textZh: 我看见各样的劳碌和各样精巧的工作，都是出于人与人彼此的竞争。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看见各样的劳碌和各样精巧的工作，都是出于人与人彼此的竞争。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又见人为一切的劳碌和各样灵巧的工作就被邻舍嫉妒。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: And I saw that all toil and all achievement spring from one person’s envy of another. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: Then I saw that all toil and all skill in work come from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: Again, I saw that for all toil and every skillful work a man is envied by his neighbor. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: Then I observed that most people are motivated to success because they envy their neighbors. But this, too, is meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen that every labor and every skill which is done is the result of rivalry between a person and his neighbor. This too is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: And I saw that all toil and all achievement spring from one person’s envy of another. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。
verses.textZhCuv: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。
verses.textEnNiv: Fools fold their hands and ruin themselves.
verses.textEnEsv: The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh.
verses.textEnNkjv: The fool folds his hands And consumes his own flesh.
verses.textEnNlt: "Fools fold their idle hands, leading them to ruin."
verses.textEnNasb: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
verses.textEn: Fools fold their hands and ruin themselves.

verses.textZh: 一掌盛满安宁，胜过两手抓满劳碌捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 一掌盛满安宁，胜过两手抓满劳碌捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 满了一把，得享安静，强如满了两把，劳碌捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: Better one handful with tranquillity than two handfuls with toil and chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: Better is a handful of quietness than two hands full of toil and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: Better a handful with quietness Than both hands full, togetherwith toil and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: And yet, "Better to have one handful with quietness than two handfuls with hard work and chasing the wind."
verses.textEnNasb: One hand full of rest is better than two fists full of labor and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: Better one handful with tranquillity than two handfuls with toil and chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 我又看到日光之下有一件虚空的事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我又看到日光之下有一件虚空的事。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又转念，见日光之下有一件虚空的事：
verses.textEnNiv: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:
verses.textEnEsv: Again, I saw vanity under the sun:
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun:
verses.textEnNlt: I observed yet another example of something meaningless under the sun.
verses.textEnNasb: Then I looked again at futility under the sun.
verses.textEn: Again I saw something meaningless under the sun:

verses.textZh: 有人孤单无依，没有儿子，没有兄弟，仍劳碌不休，眼目也不以自己的财富为足。他问："我劳劳碌碌，刻薄自己不去享受，是为谁呢？" 这也是虚空，是劳苦的担子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有人孤单无依，没有儿子，没有兄弟，仍劳碌不休，眼目也不以自己的财富为足。他问："我劳劳碌碌，刻薄自己不去享受，是为谁呢？" 这也是虚空，是劳苦的担子。
verses.textZhCuv: 有人孤单无二，无子无兄，竟劳碌不息，眼目也不以钱财为足。他说：「我劳劳碌碌，刻苦自己，不享福乐，到底是为谁呢？」这也是虚空，是极重的劳苦。
verses.textEnNiv: There was a man all alone; he had neither son nor brother. There was no end to his toil, yet his eyes were not content with his wealth. "For whom am I toiling," he asked, "and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?" This too is meaningless— a miserable business!
verses.textEnEsv: one person who has no other, either son or brother, yet there is no end to all his toil, and his eyes are never satisfied with riches, so that he never asks, "For whom am I toiling and depriving myself of pleasure?" This also is vanity and an unhappy business.
verses.textEnNkjv: There is one alone, without companion: He has neither son nor brother. Yet thereis no end to all his labors, Nor is his eye satisfied with riches. But he never asks, "For whom do I toil and deprive myself of good?" This also is vanity and a grave misfortune.
verses.textEnNlt: This is the case of a man who is all alone, without a child or a brother, yet who works hard to gain as much wealth as he can. But then he asks himself, "Who am I working for? Why am I giving up so much pleasure now?" It is all so meaningless and depressing.
verses.textEnNasb: There was a man without a dependent, having neither a son nor a brother, yet there was no end to all his labor. Indeed, his eyes were not satisfied with riches, and he never asked, "And for whom do I labor and deprive myself of pleasure?" This too is futility, and it is an unhappy task.
verses.textEn: There was a man all alone; he had neither son nor brother. There was no end to his toil, yet his eyes were not content with his wealth. "For whom am I toiling," he asked, "and why am I depriving myself of enjoyment?" This too is meaningless— a miserable business!

verses.textZh: 二人胜过一人，因为他们一起的劳碌有美好的酬报。
verses.textZhCnvs: 二人胜过一人，因为他们一起的劳碌有美好的酬报。
verses.textZhCuv: 两个人总比一个人好，因为二人劳碌同得美好的果效。
verses.textEnNiv: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor:
verses.textEnEsv: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
verses.textEnNkjv: Two are better than one, Because they have a good reward for their labor.
verses.textEnNlt: Two people are better off than one, for they can help each other succeed.
verses.textEnNasb: Two are better than one because they have a good return for their labor;
verses.textEn: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor:

verses.textZh: 如果一个跌倒，另一个可以把他的同伴扶起来。但一人孤身跌倒，没有别人把他扶起来，他就悲惨了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果一个跌倒，另一个可以把他的同伴扶起来。但一人孤身跌倒，没有别人把他扶起来，他就悲惨了。
verses.textZhCuv: 若是跌倒，这人可以扶起他的同伴；若是孤身跌倒，没有别人扶起他来，这人就有祸了。
verses.textEnNiv: If either of them falls down, one can help the other up. But pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them up.
verses.textEnEsv: For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. But woe to him who is alone when he falls and has not another to lift him up!
verses.textEnNkjv: For if they fall, one will lift up his companion. But woe to him whois alone when he falls, For hehas no one to help him up.
verses.textEnNlt: If one person falls, the other can reach out and help. But someone who falls alone is in real trouble.
verses.textEnNasb: for if either of them falls, the one will lift up his companion. But woe to the one who falls when there is not another to lift him up!
verses.textEn: If either of them falls down, one can help the other up. But pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them up.

verses.textZh: 还有，二人同睡，就都暖和；一人独睡，怎能暖和呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 还有，二人同睡，就都暖和；一人独睡，怎能暖和呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 再者，二人同睡就都暖和，一人独睡怎能暖和呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?
verses.textEnEsv: Again, if two lie together, they keep warm, but how can one keep warm alone?
verses.textEnNkjv: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; But how can one be warm alone?
verses.textEnNlt: Likewise, two people lying close together can keep each other warm. But how can one be warm alone?
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, if two lie down together they keep warm, but how can one be warm alone?
verses.textEn: Also, if two lie down together, they will keep warm. But how can one keep warm alone?

verses.textZh: 有人能制伏孤身一人，如果有二人就挡得住他。三股合成的绳子，不容易扯断。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有人能制伏孤身一人，如果有二人就挡得住他。三股合成的绳子，不容易扯断。
verses.textZhCuv: 有人攻胜孤身一人，若有二人便能敌挡他；三股合成的绳子不容易折断。
verses.textEnNiv: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
verses.textEnEsv: And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him—a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.textEnNkjv: Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.textEnNlt: A person standing alone can be attacked and defeated, but two can stand back-to-back and conquer. Three are even better, for a triple-braided cord is not easily broken.
verses.textEnNasb: And if one can overpower him who is alone, two can resist him. A cord of three strands is not quickly torn apart.
verses.textEn: Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

verses.textZh: 贫穷但有智慧的年轻人，胜过年老不再纳谏的愚昧王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 贫穷但有智慧的年轻人，胜过年老不再纳谏的愚昧王。
verses.textZhCuv: 贫穷而有智慧的少年人胜过年老不肯纳谏的愚昧王。
verses.textEnNiv: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to heed a warning.
verses.textEnEsv: Better was a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knew how to take advice.
verses.textEnNkjv: Better a poor and wise youth Than an old and foolish king who will be admonished no more.
verses.textEnNlt: It is better to be a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king who refuses all advice.
verses.textEnNasb: A poor yet wise youth is better than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to receive instruction—
verses.textEn: Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to heed a warning.

verses.textZh: 虽然他是从监狱出来，在自己的国中，又是出身贫寒，却起来作王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 虽然他是从监狱出来，在自己的国中，又是出身贫寒，却起来作王。
verses.textZhCuv: 这人是从监牢中出来作王，在他国中，生来原是贫穷的。
verses.textEnNiv: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.
verses.textEnEsv: For he went from prison to the throne, though in his own kingdom he had been born poor.
verses.textEnNkjv: For he comes out of prison to be king, Although he was born poor in his kingdom.
verses.textEnNlt: Such a youth could rise from poverty and succeed. He might even become king, though he has been in prison.
verses.textEnNasb: for he has come out of prison to become king, even though he was born poor in his kingdom.
verses.textEn: The youth may have come from prison to the kingship, or he may have been born in poverty within his kingdom.

verses.textZh: 我看见所有在日光之下行走的活人，都随从那取代老王的年轻人 。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看见所有在日光之下行走的活人，都随从那取代老王的年轻人 。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下一切行动的活人都随从那第二位，就是起来代替老王的少年人。
verses.textEnNiv: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king’s successor.
verses.textEnEsv: I saw all the living who move about under the sun, along with that youth who was to stand in the king’s place.
verses.textEnNkjv: I saw all the living who walk under the sun; They were with the second youth who stands in his place.
verses.textEnNlt: But then everyone rushes to the side of yet another youth who replaces him.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen all those living under the sun move to the side of the second youth who replaces him.
verses.textEn: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed the youth, the king’s successor.

verses.textZh: 所有的人民，就是他所统治的人民，多得无数；然而后来的人却不喜欢他。这实在也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 所有的人民，就是他所统治的人民，多得无数；然而后来的人却不喜欢他。这实在也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 他所治理的众人就是他的百姓，多得无数；在他后来的人尚且不喜悦他。这真是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: There was no end of all the people, all of whom he led. Yet those who come later will not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therewas no end of all the people over whom he was made king; Yet those who come afterward will not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: Endless crowds stand around him, but then another generation grows up and rejects him, too. So it is all meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them. Even the ones who will come later will not be happy with him; for this too is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: There was no end to all the people who were before them. But those who came later were not pleased with the successor. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 你到神的殿，脚步要谨慎；近前聆听，胜于愚昧人献祭，因为他们不知道所作的是恶的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你到神的殿，脚步要谨慎；近前聆听，胜于愚昧人献祭，因为他们不知道所作的是恶的。
verses.textZhCuv: 你到神的殿要谨慎脚步；因为近前听，胜过愚昧人献祭 ，他们本不知道所做的是恶。
verses.textEnNiv: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
verses.textEnEsv: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. To draw near to listen is better than to offer the sacrifice of fools, for they do not know that they are doing evil.
verses.textEnNkjv: Walk prudently when you go to the house of God; and draw near to hear rather than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they do not know that they do evil.
verses.textEnNlt: As you enter the house of God, keep your ears open and your mouth shut. It is evil to make mindless offerings to God.
verses.textEnNasb: Guard your steps as you go to the house of God, and approach to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools; for they do not know that they are doing evil.
verses.textEn: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Go near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.

verses.textZh: 在神面前不可冒失开口，心急发言，因为神在天上，你在地上，所以你的言语要寡少。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在神面前不可冒失开口，心急发言，因为神在天上，你在地上，所以你的言语要寡少。
verses.textZhCuv: 你在神面前不可冒失开口，也不可心急发言；因为神在天上，你在地下，所以你的言语要寡少。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not be quick with your mouth, do not be hasty in your heart to utter anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.
