verses.textEnEsv: Be not rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be hasty to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not be rash with your mouth, And let not your heart utter anything hastily before God. For God is in heaven, and you on earth; Therefore let your words be few.
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t make rash promises, and don’t be hasty in bringing matters before God. After all, God is in heaven, and you are here on earth. So let your words be few.
verses.textEnNasb: Do not be quick with your mouth or impulsive in thought to bring up a matter in the presence of God. For God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few.
verses.textEn: Do not be quick with your mouth, do not be hasty in your heart to utter anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.

verses.textZh: 挂虑多就令人作梦，言语多就显出愚昧。
verses.textZhCnvs: 挂虑多就令人作梦，言语多就显出愚昧。
verses.textZhCuv: 事务多，就令人做梦；言语多，就显出愚昧。
verses.textEnNiv: A dream comes when there are many cares, and many words mark the speech of a fool.
verses.textEnEsv: For a dream comes with much business, and a fool’s voice with many words.
verses.textEnNkjv: For a dream comes through much activity, And a fool’s voice isknown by his many words.
verses.textEnNlt: Too much activity gives you restless dreams; too many words make you a fool.
verses.textEnNasb: For the dream comes through much effort, and the voice of a fool through many words.
verses.textEn: A dream comes when there are many cares, and many words mark the speech of a fool.

verses.textZh: 你向神许了愿，就不可迟迟不还，因为他不喜悦愚昧人；所许的愿必须偿还。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你向神许了愿，就不可迟迟不还，因为他不喜悦愚昧人；所许的愿必须偿还。
verses.textZhCuv: 你向神许愿，偿还不可迟延，因他不喜悦愚昧人，所以你许的愿应当偿还。
verses.textEnNiv: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.
verses.textEnEsv: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay what you vow.
verses.textEnNkjv: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to pay it; For Hehas no pleasure in fools. Pay what you have vowed—
verses.textEnNlt: When you make a promise to God, don’t delay in following through, for God takes no pleasure in fools. Keep all the promises you make to him.
verses.textEnNasb: When you make a vow to God, do not be late in paying it; for He takes no delight in fools. Pay what you vow!
verses.textEn: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow.

verses.textZh: 许愿不还，不如不许。
verses.textZhCnvs: 许愿不还，不如不许。
verses.textZhCuv: 你许愿不还，不如不许。
verses.textEnNiv: It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.
verses.textEnEsv: It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay.
verses.textEnNkjv: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay.
verses.textEnNlt: It is better to say nothing than to make a promise and not keep it.
verses.textEnNasb: It is better that you not vow, than vow and not pay.
verses.textEn: It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.

verses.textZh: 不可任你的口使自己犯罪，也不可在使者前面说是许错了。何必使神因你的声音发怒，破坏你手中的工作呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 不可任你的口使自己犯罪，也不可在使者前面说是许错了。何必使神因你的声音发怒，破坏你手中的工作呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 不可任你的口使肉体犯罪，也不可在祭司 面前说是错许了。为何使神因你的声音发怒，败坏你手所做的呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the temple messenger, "My vow was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.textEnEsv: Let not your mouth lead you into sin, and do not say before the messenger that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the messenger ofGod that it was an error. Why should God be angry at your excuse and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t let your mouth make you sin. And don’t defend yourself by telling the Temple messenger that the promise you made was a mistake. That would make God angry, and he might wipe out everything you have achieved.
verses.textEnNasb: Do not let your speech cause you to sin, and do not say in the presence of the messenger of God that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry on account of your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.textEn: Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the temple messenger, "My vow was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands?

verses.textZh: 多梦和多话，都是虚空的，你只要敬畏神。
verses.textZhCnvs: 多梦和多话，都是虚空的，你只要敬畏神。
verses.textZhCuv: 多梦和多言，其中多有虚幻，你只要敬畏神。
verses.textEnNiv: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore fear God.
verses.textEnEsv: For when dreams increase and words grow many, there is vanity; but God is the one you must fear.
verses.textEnNkjv: For in the multitude of dreams and many words thereis also vanity. But fear God.
verses.textEnNlt: Talk is cheap, like daydreams and other useless activities. Fear God instead.
verses.textEnNasb: For in many dreams and in many words there is futility. Rather, fear God.
verses.textEn: Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore fear God.

verses.textZh: 如果你在一省之中，看到穷人遭受欺压，公正和公义被夺去，也不必因此惊讶，因为高位者之上有较高的照应，在他们之上还有更高的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果你在一省之中，看到穷人遭受欺压，公正和公义被夺去，也不必因此惊讶，因为高位者之上有较高的照应，在他们之上还有更高的。
verses.textZhCuv: 你若在一省之中见穷人受欺压，并夺去公义公平的事，不要因此诧异；因有一位高过居高位的鉴察，在他们以上还有更高的。
verses.textEnNiv: If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.
verses.textEnEsv: If you see in a province the oppression of the poor and the violation of justice and righteousness, do not be amazed at the matter, for the high official is watched by a higher, and there are yet higher ones over them.
verses.textEnNkjv: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent perversion of justice and righteousness in a province, do not marvel at the matter; for high official watches over high official, and higher officials are over them.
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t be surprised if you see a poor person being oppressed by the powerful and if justice is being miscarried throughout the land. For every official is under orders from higher up, and matters of justice get lost in red tape and bureaucracy.
verses.textEnNasb: If you see oppression of the poor and denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be shocked at the sight; for one official watches over another official, and there are higher officials over them.
verses.textEn: If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is eyed by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still.

verses.textZh: 各人都从土地得着利益，就是君王也得到田地的供应。
verses.textZhCnvs: 各人都从土地得着利益，就是君王也得到田地的供应。
verses.textZhCuv: 况且地的益处归众人，就是君王也受田地的供应。
verses.textEnNiv: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
verses.textEnEsv: But this is gain for a land in every way: a king committed to cultivated fields.
verses.textEnNkjv: Moreover the profit of the land is for all; even the king is served from the field.
verses.textEnNlt: Even the king milks the land for his own profit!
verses.textEnNasb: After all, a king who cultivates the field is beneficial to the land.
verses.textEn: The increase from the land is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.

verses.textZh: 贪爱银子的，不因有银子满足；贪爱财富的，也不因得利知足。这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 贪爱银子的，不因有银子满足；贪爱财富的，也不因得利知足。这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 贪爱银子的，不因得银子知足；贪爱丰富的，也不因得利益知足。这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: Whoever loves money never has enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with their income. This too is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: He who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor he who loves wealth with his income; this also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; Nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: Those who love money will never have enough. How meaningless to think that wealth brings true happiness!
verses.textEnNasb: One who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor one who loves abundance with its income. This too is futility.
verses.textEn: Whoever loves money never has enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with their income. This too is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 财物增加，吃用的人也增加，物主除了眼看以外，还有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 财物增加，吃用的人也增加，物主除了眼看以外，还有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 货物增添，吃的人也增添，物主得什么益处呢？不过眼看而已！
verses.textEnNiv: As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owners except to feast their eyes on them?
verses.textEnEsv: When goods increase, they increase who eat them, and what advantage has their owner but to see them with his eyes?
verses.textEnNkjv: When goods increase, They increase who eat them; So what profit have the owners Except to see them with their eyes?
verses.textEnNlt: The more you have, the more people come to help you spend it. So what good is wealth—except perhaps to watch it slip through your fingers!
verses.textEnNasb: When good things increase, those who consume them increase. So what is the advantage to their owners except to look at them?
verses.textEn: As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owners except to feast their eyes on them?

verses.textZh: 劳力的人无论吃多吃少，都睡得甜；财主的丰足，却不容他安睡。
verses.textZhCnvs: 劳力的人无论吃多吃少，都睡得甜；财主的丰足，却不容他安睡。
verses.textZhCuv: 劳碌的人不拘吃多吃少，睡得香甜；富足人的丰满却不容他睡觉。
verses.textEnNiv: The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether they eat little or much, but as for the rich, their abundance permits them no sleep.
verses.textEnEsv: Sweet is the sleep of a laborer, whether he eats little or much, but the full stomach of the rich will not let him sleep.
verses.textEnNkjv: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, Whether he eats little or much; But the abundance of the rich will not permit him to sleep.
verses.textEnNlt: People who work hard sleep well, whether they eat little or much. But the rich seldom get a good night’s sleep.
verses.textEnNasb: The sleep of the laborer is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the full stomach of the rich person does not allow him to sleep.
verses.textEn: The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether they eat little or much, but as for the rich, their abundance permits them no sleep.

verses.textZh: 我看见日光之下有一令人痛心的憾事，就是财主积聚财富，反受其害。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看见日光之下有一令人痛心的憾事，就是财主积聚财富，反受其害。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下有一宗大祸患，就是财主积存资财，反害自己。
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owners,
verses.textEnEsv: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: riches were kept by their owner to his hurt,
verses.textEnNkjv: There is a severe evil which I have seen under the sun: Riches kept for their owner to his hurt.
verses.textEnNlt: There is another serious problem I have seen under the sun. Hoarding riches harms the saver.
verses.textEnNasb: There is a sickening evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth being hoarded by its owner to his detriment.
verses.textEn: I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owners,

verses.textZh: 遭遇祸患，财富就尽失；他即使生了儿子，也没有甚么留给他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 遭遇祸患，财富就尽失；他即使生了儿子，也没有甚么留给他。
verses.textZhCuv: 因遭遇祸患，这些资财就消灭；那人若生了儿子，手里也一无所有。
verses.textEnNiv: or wealth lost through some misfortune, so that when they have children there is nothing left for them to inherit.
verses.textEnEsv: and those riches were lost in a bad venture. And he is father of a son, but he has nothing in his hand.
verses.textEnNkjv: But those riches perish through misfortune; When he begets a son, thereis nothing in his hand.
verses.textEnNlt: Money is put into risky investments that turn sour, and everything is lost. In the end, there is nothing left to pass on to one’s children.
verses.textEnNasb: When that wealth was lost through bad business and he had fathered a son, then there was nothing to support him.
verses.textEn: or wealth lost through some misfortune, so that when they have children there is nothing left for them to inherit.

verses.textZh: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必怎样赤身而去；在劳碌中得来的，他的手也带不走甚么。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必怎样赤身而去；在劳碌中得来的，他的手也带不走甚么。
verses.textZhCuv: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必照样赤身而去；他所劳碌得来的，手中分毫不能带去。
verses.textEnNiv: Everyone comes naked from their mother’s womb, and as everyone comes, so they depart. They take nothing from their toil that they can carry in their hands.
verses.textEnEsv: As he came from his mother’s womb he shall go again, naked as he came, and shall take nothing for his toil that he may carry away in his hand.
verses.textEnNkjv: As he came from his mother’s womb, naked shall he return, To go as he came; And he shall take nothing from his labor Which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.textEnNlt: We all come to the end of our lives as naked and empty-handed as on the day we were born. We can’t take our riches with us.
verses.textEnNasb: As he came naked from his mother’s womb, so he will return as he came. He will take nothing from the fruit of his labor that he can carry in his hand.
verses.textEn: Everyone comes naked from their mother’s womb, and as everyone comes, so they depart. They take nothing from their toil that they can carry in their hands.

verses.textZh: 他怎样来，也要怎样去，这也是令人痛心的憾事；他为风劳碌，有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 他怎样来，也要怎样去，这也是令人痛心的憾事；他为风劳碌，有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 他来的情形怎样，他去的情形也怎样。这也是一宗大祸患。他为风劳碌有什么益处呢？
verses.textEnNiv: This too is a grievous evil: As everyone comes, so they depart, and what do they gain, since they toil for the wind?
verses.textEnEsv: This also is a grievous evil: just as he came, so shall he go, and what gain is there to him who toils for the wind?
verses.textEnNkjv: And this also is a severe evil— Just exactly as he came, so shall he go. And what profit has he who has labored for the wind?
verses.textEnNlt: And this, too, is a very serious problem. People leave this world no better off than when they came. All their hard work is for nothing—like working for the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: This also is a sickening evil: exactly as a person is born, so will he die. What then is the advantage for him who labors for the wind?
verses.textEn: This too is a grievous evil: As everyone comes, so they depart, and what do they gain, since they toil for the wind?

verses.textZh: 他终生在黑暗中吃喝，多有愁烦、疾病与愤怨。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他终生在黑暗中吃喝，多有愁烦、疾病与愤怨。
verses.textZhCuv: 并且他终身在黑暗中吃喝，多有烦恼，又有病患呕气。
verses.textEnNiv: All their days they eat in darkness, with great frustration, affliction and anger.
verses.textEnEsv: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness in much vexation and sickness and anger.
verses.textEnNkjv: All his days he also eats in darkness, And hehas much sorrow and sickness and anger.
verses.textEnNlt: Throughout their lives, they live under a cloud—frustrated, discouraged, and angry.
verses.textEnNasb: All his life he also eats in darkness with great irritation, sickness, and anger.
verses.textEn: All their days they eat in darkness, with great frustration, affliction and anger.

verses.textZh: 我认为既善又美的，就是人在神所赐给他一生有限的年日中吃喝，享受他在日光之下劳碌所得的一切，因为这是他的分。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我认为既善又美的，就是人在神所赐给他一生有限的年日中吃喝，享受他在日光之下劳碌所得的一切，因为这是他的分。
verses.textZhCuv: 我所见为善为美的，就是人在神赐他一生的日子吃喝，享受日光之下劳碌得来的好处，因为这是他的分。
verses.textEnNiv: This is what I have observed to be good: that it is appropriate for a person to eat, to drink and to find satisfaction in their toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given them—for this is their lot.
verses.textEnEsv: Behold, what I have seen to be good and fitting is to eat and drink and find enjoyment in all the toil with which one toils under the sun the few days of his life that God has given him, for this is his lot.
verses.textEnNkjv: Here is what I have seen: Itis good and fitting forone to eat and drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor in which he toils under the sun all the days of his life which God gives him; for it is his heritage.
verses.textEnNlt: Even so, I have noticed one thing, at least, that is good. It is good for people to eat, drink, and enjoy their work under the sun during the short life God has given them, and to accept their lot in life.
verses.textEnNasb: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat, to drink, and enjoy oneself in all one’s labor in which he labors under the sun during the few years of his life which God has given him; for this is his reward.
verses.textEn: This is what I have observed to be good: that it is appropriate for a person to eat, to drink and to find satisfaction in their toilsome labor under the sun during the few days of life God has given them—for this is their lot.

verses.textZh: 蒙神赐予财富与资产的人，神都使他能够享用，并取自己的分，在劳碌中自得其乐，这是神的恩赐。
verses.textZhCnvs: 蒙神赐予财富与资产的人，神都使他能够享用，并取自己的分，在劳碌中自得其乐，这是神的恩赐。
verses.textZhCuv: 神赐人资财丰富，使他能以吃用，能取自己的分，在他劳碌中喜乐，这乃是神的恩赐。
verses.textEnNiv: Moreover, when God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the ability to enjoy them, to accept their lot and be happy in their toil—this is a gift of God.
verses.textEnEsv: Everyone also to whom God has given wealth and possessions and power to enjoy them, and to accept his lot and rejoice in his toil—this is the gift of God.
verses.textEnNkjv: As for every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and given him power to eat of it, to receive his heritage and rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
verses.textEnNlt: And it is a good thing to receive wealth from God and the good health to enjoy it. To enjoy your work and accept your lot in life—this is indeed a gift from God.
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, as for every person to whom God has given riches and wealth, He has also given him the opportunity to enjoy them and to receive his reward and rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God.
verses.textEn: Moreover, when God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the ability to enjoy them, to accept their lot and be happy in their toil—this is a gift of God.

verses.textZh: 他不多思念自己一生的年日，因为神使喜乐充满他的心。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他不多思念自己一生的年日，因为神使喜乐充满他的心。
verses.textZhCuv: 他不多思念自己一生的年日，因为神应他的心使他喜乐。
verses.textEnNiv: They seldom reflect on the days of their life, because God keeps them occupied with gladness of heart.
verses.textEnEsv: For he will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with joy in his heart.
verses.textEnNkjv: For he will not dwell unduly on the days of his life, because God keeps him busy with the joy of his heart.
verses.textEnNlt: God keeps such people so busy enjoying life that they take no time to brood over the past.
verses.textEnNasb: For he will not often call to mind the years of his life, because God keeps him busy with the joy of his heart.
verses.textEn: They seldom reflect on the days of their life, because God keeps them occupied with gladness of heart.

verses.textZh: 我看见日光之下有一件憾事，重压在世人身上。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看见日光之下有一件憾事，重压在世人身上。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下有一宗祸患重压在人身上，
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on mankind:
verses.textEnEsv: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on mankind:
verses.textEnNkjv: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
verses.textEnNlt: There is another serious tragedy I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily on humanity.
verses.textEnNasb: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is widespread among mankind:
verses.textEn: I have seen another evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on mankind:

verses.textZh: 蒙神赐予财富、资产和荣誉的人，心里所愿的，都一无所缺，可是神使他无力享用，反而有外人来享用。这是虚空，也是祸患。
verses.textZhCnvs: 蒙神赐予财富、资产和荣誉的人，心里所愿的，都一无所缺，可是神使他无力享用，反而有外人来享用。这是虚空，也是祸患。
verses.textZhCuv: 就是人蒙神赐他资财、丰富、尊荣，以致他心里所愿的一样都不缺，只是神使他不能吃用，反有外人来吃用。这是虚空，也是祸患。
verses.textEnNiv: God gives some people wealth, possessions and honor, so that they lack nothing their hearts desire, but God does not grant them the ability to enjoy them, and strangers enjoy them instead. This is meaningless, a grievous evil.
verses.textEnEsv: a man to whom God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, so that he lacks nothing of all that he desires, yet God does not give him power to enjoy them, but a stranger enjoys them. This is vanity; it is a grievous evil.
verses.textEnNkjv: A man to whom God has given riches and wealth and honor, so that he lacks nothing for himself of all he desires; yet God does not give him power to eat of it, but a foreigner consumes it. This is vanity, and it is an evil affliction.
verses.textEnNlt: God gives some people great wealth and honor and everything they could ever want, but then he doesn’t give them the chance to enjoy these things. They die, and someone else, even a stranger, ends up enjoying their wealth! This is meaningless—a sickening tragedy.
verses.textEnNasb: a person to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that his soul lacks nothing of all that he desires, yet God has not given him the opportunity to enjoy these things, but a foreigner enjoys them. This is futility and a severe affliction.
verses.textEn: God gives some people wealth, possessions and honor, so that they lack nothing their hearts desire, but God does not grant them the ability to enjoy them, and strangers enjoy them instead. This is meaningless, a grievous evil.

verses.textZh: 人如果生下百子，活了许多岁数，年日长久，但是心里不因美物满足，又得不到安葬，我以为流产的胎比他还好。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人如果生下百子，活了许多岁数，年日长久，但是心里不因美物满足，又得不到安葬，我以为流产的胎比他还好。
verses.textZhCuv: 人若生一百个儿子，活许多岁数，以致他的年日甚多，心里却不得满享福乐，又不得埋葬；据我说，那不到期而落的胎比他倒好。
verses.textEnNiv: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
verses.textEnEsv: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not satisfied with life’s good things, and he also has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
verses.textEnNkjv: If a man begets a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not satisfied with goodness, or indeed he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he—
verses.textEnNlt: A man might have a hundred children and live to be very old. But if he finds no satisfaction in life and doesn’t even get a decent burial, it would have been better for him to be born dead.
verses.textEnNasb: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, however many they may be, but his soul is not satisfied with good things and he does not even have a proper burial, then I say, "Better the miscarriage than he,
verses.textEn: A man may have a hundred children and live many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he cannot enjoy his prosperity and does not receive proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

verses.textZh: 因为这胎虚虚而来，暗暗而去，黑暗把他的名字遮蔽了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为这胎虚虚而来，暗暗而去，黑暗把他的名字遮蔽了。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为虚虚而来，暗暗而去，名字被黑暗遮蔽，
verses.textEnNiv: It comes without meaning, it departs in darkness, and in darkness its name is shrouded.
verses.textEnEsv: For it comes in vanity and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name is covered.
verses.textEnNkjv: for it comes in vanity and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
verses.textEnNlt: His birth would have been meaningless, and he would have ended in darkness. He wouldn’t even have had a name,
verses.textEnNasb: for a miscarriage comes in futility and goes into darkness; and its name is covered in darkness.
verses.textEn: It comes without meaning, it departs in darkness, and in darkness its name is shrouded.

verses.textZh: 这胎既看不见天日，又一无所知，就比那人更得安息。
verses.textZhCnvs: 这胎既看不见天日，又一无所知，就比那人更得安息。
verses.textZhCuv: 并且没有见过天日，也毫无知觉；这胎，比那人倒享安息。
verses.textEnNiv: Though it never saw the sun or knew anything, it has more rest than does that man—
verses.textEnEsv: Moreover, it has not seen the sun or known anything, yet it finds rest rather than he.
verses.textEnNkjv: Though it has not seen the sun or known anything, this has more rest than that man,
verses.textEnNlt: and he would never have seen the sun or known of its existence. Yet he would have had more peace than in growing up to be an unhappy man.
verses.textEnNasb: It has not even seen the sun nor does it know it; yet it is better off than that man.
verses.textEn: Though it never saw the sun or knew anything, it has more rest than does that man—

verses.textZh: 那人即使活了一千年，再活一千年，也享受不到甚么；他们两者不是都归一个地方吗？
verses.textZhCnvs: 那人即使活了一千年，再活一千年，也享受不到甚么；他们两者不是都归一个地方吗？
verses.textZhCuv: 那人虽然活千年，再活千年，却不享福，众人岂不都归一个地方去吗？
verses.textEnNiv: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
verses.textEnEsv: Even though he should live a thousand years twice over, yet enjoy no good—do not all go to the one place?
verses.textEnNkjv: even if he lives a thousand years twice—but has not seen goodness. Do not all go to one place?
verses.textEnNlt: He might live a thousand years twice over but still not find contentment. And since he must die like everyone else—well, what’s the use?
verses.textEnNasb: Even if the man lives a thousand years twice, but does not see good things—do not all go to one and the same place?"
verses.textEn: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

verses.textZh: 人的一切劳碌都为口腹，他的心却还是填不满。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人的一切劳碌都为口腹，他的心却还是填不满。
verses.textZhCuv: 人的劳碌都为口腹，心里却不知足。
verses.textEnNiv: Everyone’s toil is for their mouth, yet their appetite is never satisfied.
verses.textEnEsv: All the toil of man is for his mouth, yet his appetite is not satisfied.
verses.textEnNkjv: All the labor of man is for his mouth, And yet the soul is not satisfied.
verses.textEnNlt: All people spend their lives scratching for food, but they never seem to have enough.
verses.textEnNasb: All a person’s labor is for his mouth, and yet his appetite is not satisfied.
verses.textEn: Everyone’s toil is for their mouth, yet their appetite is never satisfied.

verses.textZh: 智慧人比愚昧人有甚么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道怎样行事为人，又有甚么长处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人比愚昧人有甚么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道怎样行事为人，又有甚么长处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 这样看来，智慧人比愚昧人有什么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道如何行，有什么长处呢？
verses.textEnNiv: What advantage have the wise over fools? What do the poor gain by knowing how to conduct themselves before others?
verses.textEnEsv: For what advantage has the wise man over the fool? And what does the poor man have who knows how to conduct himself before the living?
verses.textEnNkjv: For what more has the wise man than the fool? What does the poor man have, Who knows how to walk before the living?
verses.textEnNlt: So are wise people really better off than fools? Do poor people gain anything by being wise and knowing how to act in front of others?
verses.textEnNasb: For what advantage does the wise person have over the fool? What does the poor person have, knowing how to walk before the living?
verses.textEn: What advantage have the wise over fools? What do the poor gain by knowing how to conduct themselves before others?

verses.textZh: 眼睛看见的，胜过心中想望的。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCnvs: 眼睛看见的，胜过心中想望的。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textZhCuv: 眼睛所看的比心里妄想的倒好。这也是虚空，也是捕风。
verses.textEnNiv: Better what the eye sees than the roving of the appetite. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
verses.textEnEsv: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite: this also is vanity and a striving after wind.
verses.textEnNkjv: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
verses.textEnNlt: Enjoy what you have rather than desiring what you don’t have. Just dreaming about nice things is meaningless—like chasing the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: What the eyes see is better than what the soul desires. This too is futility and striving after wind.
verses.textEn: Better what the eye sees than the roving of the appetite. This too is meaningless, a chasing after the wind.

verses.textZh: 已经存在的，早已有了名称；大家都知道人是怎样的；人绝对无法与比自己强的抗辩。
verses.textZhCnvs: 已经存在的，早已有了名称；大家都知道人是怎样的；人绝对无法与比自己强的抗辩。
verses.textZhCuv: 先前所有的，早已起了名，并知道何为人，他也不能与那比自己力大的相争。
verses.textEnNiv: Whatever exists has already been named, and what humanity is has been known; no one can contend with someone who is stronger.
verses.textEnEsv: Whatever has come to be has already been named, and it is known what man is, and that he is not able to dispute with one stronger than he.
verses.textEnNkjv: Whatever one is, he has been named already, For it is known that he is man; And he cannot contend with Him who is mightier than he.
verses.textEnNlt: Everything has already been decided. It was known long ago what each person would be. So there’s no use arguing with God about your destiny.
verses.textEnNasb: Whatever exists has already been named, and it is known what man is; for he cannot dispute with the one who is mightier than he is.
verses.textEn: Whatever exists has already been named, and what humanity is has been known; no one can contend with someone who is stronger.

verses.textZh: 因为话语增多，虚空也增多，这对人有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为话语增多，虚空也增多，这对人有甚么益处呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 加增虚浮的事既多，这与人有什么益处呢？
verses.textEnNiv: The more the words, the less the meaning, and how does that profit anyone?
verses.textEnEsv: The more words, the more vanity, and what is the advantage to man?
verses.textEnNkjv: Since there are many things that increase vanity, How is man the better?
verses.textEnNlt: The more words you speak, the less they mean. So what good are they?
verses.textEnNasb: For there are many words which increase futility. What then is the advantage to a person?
verses.textEn: The more the words, the less the meaning, and how does that profit anyone?

verses.textZh: 在虚空、消逝如影的人生，短暂的日子里，有谁知道甚么是对人有益处呢？谁能告诉人他死后在日光之下会发生甚么事呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 在虚空、消逝如影的人生，短暂的日子里，有谁知道甚么是对人有益处呢？谁能告诉人他死后在日光之下会发生甚么事呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 人一生虚度的日子，就如影儿经过，谁知道什么与他有益呢？谁能告诉他身后在日光之下有什么事呢？
verses.textEnNiv: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the few and meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?
verses.textEnEsv: For who knows what is good for man while he lives the few days of his vain life, which he passes like a shadow? For who can tell man what will be after him under the sun?
verses.textEnNkjv: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he passes like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will happen after him under the sun?
verses.textEnNlt: In the few days of our meaningless lives, who knows how our days can best be spent? Our lives are like a shadow. Who can tell what will happen on this earth after we are gone?
verses.textEnNasb: For who knows what is good for a person during his lifetime, during the few years of his futile life? He will spend them like a shadow. For who can tell a person what will happen after him under the sun?
verses.textEn: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the few and meaningless days they pass through like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they are gone?

verses.textZh: 美名优于美好的膏油， 死亡的日子胜过诞生的日子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 美名优于美好的膏油， 死亡的日子胜过诞生的日子。
verses.textZhCuv: 名誉强如美好的膏油；人死的日子胜过人生的日子。
verses.textEnNiv: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth.
verses.textEnEsv: A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of birth.
verses.textEnNkjv: A good name is better than precious ointment, And the day of death than the day of one’s birth;
verses.textEnNlt: A good reputation is more valuable than costly perfume. And the day you die is better than the day you are born.
verses.textEnNasb: A good name is better than good oil, And the day of one’s death is better than the day of one’s birth.
verses.textEn: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death better than the day of birth.

verses.textZh: 往服丧之家，比往宴乐之家还好， 因为死是人人的结局， 活人要把这事放在心上。
verses.textZhCnvs: 往服丧之家，比往宴乐之家还好， 因为死是人人的结局， 活人要把这事放在心上。
verses.textZhCuv: 往遭丧的家去， 强如往宴乐的家去； 因为死是众人的结局， 活人也必将这事放在心上。
verses.textEnNiv: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of everyone; the living should take this to heart.
verses.textEnEsv: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.
verses.textEnNkjv: Better to go to the house of mourning Than to go to the house of feasting, For that is the end of all men; And the living will take it to heart.
verses.textEnNlt: Better to spend your time at funerals than at parties. After all, everyone dies— so the living should take this to heart.
verses.textEnNasb: It is better to go to a house of mourning Than to go to a house of feasting, Because that is the end of every person, And the living takes it to heart.
verses.textEn: It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for death is the destiny of everyone; the living should take this to heart.

verses.textZh: 忧愁胜于嬉笑， 因为面带愁容，能使内心得着好处。
verses.textZhCnvs: 忧愁胜于嬉笑， 因为面带愁容，能使内心得着好处。
verses.textZhCuv: 忧愁强如喜笑； 因为面带愁容，终必使心喜乐。
verses.textEnNiv: Frustration is better than laughter, because a sad face is good for the heart.
verses.textEnEsv: Sorrow is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad.
verses.textEnNkjv: Sorrow is better than laughter, For by a sad countenance the heart is made better.
verses.textEnNlt: Sorrow is better than laughter, for sadness has a refining influence on us.
verses.textEnNasb: Sorrow is better than laughter, For when a face is sad a heart may be happy.
verses.textEn: Frustration is better than laughter, because a sad face is good for the heart.

verses.textZh: 智慧人的心在服丧之家， 愚昧人的心在欢乐之家。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人的心在服丧之家， 愚昧人的心在欢乐之家。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人的心在遭丧之家； 愚昧人的心在快乐之家。
verses.textEnNiv: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
verses.textEnEsv: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.textEnNkjv: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, But the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
verses.textEnNlt: A wise person thinks a lot about death, while a fool thinks only about having a good time.
verses.textEnNasb: The mind of the wise is in the house of mourning, While the mind of fools is in the house of pleasure.
verses.textEn: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

verses.textZh: 听智慧人的斥责， 胜过听愚昧人的歌唱。
verses.textZhCnvs: 听智慧人的斥责， 胜过听愚昧人的歌唱。
verses.textZhCuv: 听智慧人的责备， 强如听愚昧人的歌唱。
verses.textEnNiv: It is better to heed the rebuke of a wise person than to listen to the song of fools.
verses.textEnEsv: It is better for a man to hear the rebuke of the wise than to hear the song of fools.
verses.textEnNkjv: Itis better to hear the rebuke of the wise Than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.textEnNlt: Better to be criticized by a wise person than to be praised by a fool.
verses.textEnNasb: It is better to listen to the rebuke of a wise person Than for one to listen to the song of fools.
verses.textEn: It is better to heed the rebuke of a wise person than to listen to the song of fools.

verses.textZh: 愚昧人的笑声， 就像锅底下荆棘的爆声一样。 这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人的笑声， 就像锅底下荆棘的爆声一样。 这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 愚昧人的笑声， 好像锅下烧荆棘的爆声； 这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: Like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fools; this also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: A fool’s laughter is quickly gone, like thorns crackling in a fire. This also is meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: For as the crackling of thorn bushes under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool; And this too is futility.
verses.textEn: Like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 勒索会使智慧人变为愚妄， 贿赂能败坏人心。
verses.textZhCnvs: 勒索会使智慧人变为愚妄， 贿赂能败坏人心。
verses.textZhCuv: 勒索使智慧人变为愚妄； 贿赂能败坏人的慧心。
verses.textEnNiv: Extortion turns a wise person into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
verses.textEnEsv: Surely oppression drives the wise into madness, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
verses.textEnNkjv: Surely oppression destroys a wise man’s reason, And a bribe debases the heart.
verses.textEnNlt: Extortion turns wise people into fools, and bribes corrupt the heart.
verses.textEnNasb: For oppression makes a wise person look foolish, And a bribe corrupts the heart.
verses.textEn: Extortion turns a wise person into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.

verses.textZh: 事情的结局胜于开端， 存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 事情的结局胜于开端， 存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。
verses.textZhCuv: 事情的终局强如事情的起头； 存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。
verses.textEnNiv: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride.
verses.textEnEsv: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning, and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.textEnNkjv: The end of a thing is better than its beginning; The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
verses.textEnNlt: Finishing is better than starting. Patience is better than pride.
verses.textEnNasb: The end of a matter is better than its beginning; Patience of spirit is better than arrogance of spirit.
verses.textEn: The end of a matter is better than its beginning, and patience is better than pride.

verses.textZh: 你心里不要轻易动怒， 因为恼怒留在愚昧人的胸怀中。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你心里不要轻易动怒， 因为恼怒留在愚昧人的胸怀中。
verses.textZhCuv: 你不要心里急躁恼怒， 因为恼怒存在愚昧人的怀中。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger resides in the lap of fools.
verses.textEnEsv: Be not quick in your spirit to become angry, for anger lodges in the heart of fools.
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not hasten in your spirit to be angry, For anger rests in the bosom of fools.
verses.textEnNlt: Control your temper, for anger labels you a fool.
verses.textEnNasb: Do not be eager in your spirit to be angry, For anger resides in the heart of fools.
verses.textEn: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger resides in the lap of fools.

verses.textZh: 你不要说："为甚么从前的日子胜过现在的呢？" 你这样问，不是出于智慧。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你不要说："为甚么从前的日子胜过现在的呢？" 你这样问，不是出于智慧。
verses.textZhCuv: 不要说： 先前的日子强过如今的日子， 是什么缘故呢？ 你这样问，不是出于智慧。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" For it is not wise to ask such questions.
verses.textEnEsv: Say not, "Why were the former days better than these?" For it is not from wisdom that you ask this.
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not say, "Why were the former days better than these?" For you do not inquire wisely concerning this.
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t long for "the good old days." This is not wise.
verses.textEnNasb: Do not say, "Why is it that the former days were better than these?" For it is not from wisdom that you ask about this.
verses.textEn: Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" For it is not wise to ask such questions.

verses.textZh: 智慧与产业都是好的， 对得见天日的人是有益的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧与产业都是好的， 对得见天日的人是有益的。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧和产业并好， 而且见天日的人得智慧更为有益。
verses.textEnNiv: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing and benefits those who see the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, an advantage to those who see the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, And profitable to those who see the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: Wisdom is even better when you have money. Both are a benefit as you go through life.
verses.textEnNasb: Wisdom along with an inheritance is good, And an advantage to those who see the sun.
verses.textEn: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing and benefits those who see the sun.

verses.textZh: 因为受智慧的庇护，如同受银子的庇护。 唯有智慧能保全智慧人的生命，这就是知识的益处。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为受智慧的庇护，如同受银子的庇护。 唯有智慧能保全智慧人的生命，这就是知识的益处。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为智慧护庇人， 好像银钱护庇人一样。 惟独智慧能保全智慧人的生命。 这就是知识的益处。
verses.textEnNiv: Wisdom is a shelter as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is this: Wisdom preserves those who have it.
verses.textEnEsv: For the protection of wisdom is like the protection of money, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
verses.textEnNkjv: For wisdom is a defense as money is a defense, But the excellence of knowledge isthat wisdom gives life to those who have it.
verses.textEnNlt: Wisdom and money can get you almost anything, but only wisdom can save your life.
verses.textEnNasb: For wisdom is protection just as money is protection, But the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom keeps its possessors alive.
verses.textEn: Wisdom is a shelter as money is a shelter, but the advantage of knowledge is this: Wisdom preserves those who have it.

verses.textZh: 要观察神的作为， 因为他所屈曲的， 谁能弄直呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 要观察神的作为， 因为他所屈曲的， 谁能弄直呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 你要察看神的作为； 因神使为曲的，谁能变为直呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Consider what God has done: Who can straighten what he has made crooked?
verses.textEnEsv: Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?
verses.textEnNkjv: Consider the work of God; For who can make straight what He has made crooked?
verses.textEnNlt: Accept the way God does things, for who can straighten what he has made crooked?
verses.textEnNasb: Consider the work of God, For who is able to straighten what He has bent?
verses.textEn: Consider what God has done: Who can straighten what he has made crooked?

verses.textZh: 在亨通的日子，应当享福； 遭遇患难的时候，就当省察。神使这两样并存， 为了叫人查不出未来的事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在亨通的日子，应当享福； 遭遇患难的时候，就当省察。神使这两样并存， 为了叫人查不出未来的事。
verses.textZhCuv: 遇亨通的日子你当喜乐；遭患难的日子你当思想；因为神使这两样并列，为的是叫人查不出身后有什么事。
verses.textEnNiv: When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider this: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, no one can discover anything about their future.
verses.textEnEsv: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other, so that man may not find out anything that will be after him.
verses.textEnNkjv: In the day of prosperity be joyful, But in the day of adversity consider: Surely God has appointed the one as well as the other, So that man can find out nothing thatwillcome after him.
verses.textEnNlt: Enjoy prosperity while you can, but when hard times strike, realize that both come from God. Remember that nothing is certain in this life.
verses.textEnNasb: On the day of prosperity be happy, But on the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other So that a person will not discover anything that will come after him.
verses.textEn: When times are good, be happy; but when times are bad, consider this: God has made the one as well as the other. Therefore, no one can discover anything about their future.

verses.textZh: 在我虚空的日子里，我见过这两件事：有义人行义反而灭亡，有恶人行恶倒享长寿。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在我虚空的日子里，我见过这两件事：有义人行义反而灭亡，有恶人行恶倒享长寿。
verses.textZhCuv: 有义人行义，反致灭亡；有恶人行恶，倒享长寿。这都是我在虚度之日中所见过的。
verses.textEnNiv: In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these: the righteous perishing in their righteousness, and the wicked living long in their wickedness.
verses.textEnEsv: In my vain life I have seen everything. There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evildoing.
verses.textEnNkjv: I have seen everything in my days of vanity: There is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, And there is a wicked man who prolongs life in his wickedness.
verses.textEnNlt: I have seen everything in this meaningless life, including the death of good young people and the long life of wicked people.
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen everything during my lifetime of futility; there is a righteous person who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked person who prolongs his life in his wickedness.
verses.textEn: In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these: the righteous perishing in their righteousness, and the wicked living long in their wickedness.

verses.textZh: 不要过分公义，也不要太过有智慧，何必自取灭亡呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 不要过分公义，也不要太过有智慧，何必自取灭亡呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 不要行义过分，也不要过于自逞智慧，何必自取败亡呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Do not be overrighteous, neither be overwise— why destroy yourself?
verses.textEnEsv: Be not overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not be overly righteous, Nor be overly wise: Why should you destroy yourself?
verses.textEnNlt: So don’t be too good or too wise! Why destroy yourself?
verses.textEnNasb: Do not be excessively righteous, and do not be overly wise. Why should you ruin yourself?
verses.textEn: Do not be overrighteous, neither be overwise— why destroy yourself?

verses.textZh: 不要过分作恶，也不要作愚昧人，何必时候未到就死？
verses.textZhCnvs: 不要过分作恶，也不要作愚昧人，何必时候未到就死？
verses.textZhCuv: 不要行恶过分，也不要为人愚昧，何必不到期而死呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Do not be overwicked, and do not be a fool— why die before your time?
verses.textEnEsv: Be not overly wicked, neither be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not be overly wicked, Nor be foolish: Why should you die before your time?
verses.textEnNlt: On the other hand, don’t be too wicked either. Don’t be a fool! Why die before your time?
verses.textEnNasb: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
verses.textEn: Do not be overwicked, and do not be a fool— why die before your time?

verses.textZh: 持守这个是好的，那个也不要放松，因为敬畏神的人，都必避免这两个极端。
verses.textZhCnvs: 持守这个是好的，那个也不要放松，因为敬畏神的人，都必避免这两个极端。
verses.textZhCuv: 你持守这个为美，那个也不要松手；因为敬畏神的人，必从这两样出来。
verses.textEnNiv: It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. Whoever fears God will avoid all extremes.
verses.textEnEsv: It is good that you should take hold of this, and from that withhold not your hand, for the one who fears God shall come out from both of them.
verses.textEnNkjv: Itis good that you grasp this, And also not remove your hand from the other; For he who fears God will escape them all.
verses.textEnNlt: Pay attention to these instructions, for anyone who fears God will avoid both extremes.
verses.textEnNasb: It is good that you grasp one thing while not letting go of the other; for one who fears God comes out with both of them.
verses.textEn: It is good to grasp the one and not let go of the other. Whoever fears God will avoid all extremes.

verses.textZh: 智慧使智慧人比城中十个官长更有能力。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧使智慧人比城中十个官长更有能力。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧使有智慧的人比城中十个官长更有能力。
verses.textEnNiv: Wisdom makes one wise person more powerful than ten rulers in a city.
verses.textEnEsv: Wisdom gives strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.textEnNkjv: Wisdom strengthens the wise More than ten rulers of the city.
verses.textEnNlt: One wise person is stronger than ten leading citizens of a town!
verses.textEnNasb: Wisdom strengthens a wise person more than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.textEn: Wisdom makes one wise person more powerful than ten rulers in a city.

verses.textZh: 世上实在没有一个行善而不犯罪的义人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 世上实在没有一个行善而不犯罪的义人。
verses.textZhCuv: 时常行善而不犯罪的义人，世上实在没有。
verses.textEnNiv: Indeed, there is no one on earth who is righteous, no one who does what is right and never sins.
verses.textEnEsv: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
verses.textEnNkjv: For thereis not a just man on earth who does good And does not sin.
verses.textEnNlt: Not a single person on earth is always good and never sins.
verses.textEnNasb: Indeed, there is not a righteous person on earth who always does good and does not ever sin.
verses.textEn: Indeed, there is no one on earth who is righteous, no one who does what is right and never sins.

verses.textZh: 人所说的一切话，都不要放在心上，因你可能听见仆人咒骂你。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人所说的一切话，都不要放在心上，因你可能听见仆人咒骂你。
verses.textZhCuv: 人所说的一切话，你不要放在心上，恐怕听见你的仆人咒诅你。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you—
verses.textEnEsv: Do not take to heart all the things that people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
verses.textEnNkjv: Also do not take to heart everything people say, Lest you hear your servant cursing you.
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t eavesdrop on others—you may hear your servant curse you.
verses.textEnNasb: Also, do not take seriously all the words which are spoken, so that you do not hear your servant cursing you,
verses.textEn: Do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you—

verses.textZh: 其实你心里明白，自己也曾多次咒骂别人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 其实你心里明白，自己也曾多次咒骂别人。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为你心里知道，自己也曾屡次咒诅别人。
verses.textEnNiv: for you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
verses.textEnEsv: Your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others.
verses.textEnNkjv: For many times, also, your own heart has known That even you have cursed others.
verses.textEnNlt: For you know how often you yourself have cursed others.
verses.textEnNasb: for you know that even you have cursed others many times as well.
verses.textEn: for you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.

verses.textZh: 这一切我都用智慧试验过。我说："我要得智慧"，智慧却远离我。
verses.textZhCnvs: 这一切我都用智慧试验过。我说："我要得智慧"，智慧却远离我。
verses.textZhCuv: 我曾用智慧试验这一切事；我说，要得智慧，智慧却离我远。
verses.textEnNiv: All this I tested by wisdom and I said, "I am determined to be wise"— but this was beyond me.
verses.textEnEsv: All this I have tested by wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was far from me.
verses.textEnNkjv: All this I have proved by wisdom. I said, "I will be wise"; But it was far from me.
verses.textEnNlt: I have always tried my best to let wisdom guide my thoughts and actions. I said to myself, "I am determined to be wise." But it didn’t work.
verses.textEnNasb: I tested all this with wisdom, and I said, "I will be wise," but wisdom was far from me.
verses.textEn: All this I tested by wisdom and I said, "I am determined to be wise"— but this was beyond me.

verses.textZh: 那离得远又极深奥的，谁能找到呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 那离得远又极深奥的，谁能找到呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 万事之理，离我甚远，而且最深，谁能测透呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Whatever exists is far off and most profound— who can discover it?
verses.textEnEsv: That which has been is far off, and deep, very deep; who can find it out?
verses.textEnNkjv: As for that which is far off and exceedingly deep, Who can find it out?
verses.textEnNlt: Wisdom is always distant and difficult to find.
verses.textEnNasb: What has been is remote and very mysterious. Who can discover it?
verses.textEn: Whatever exists is far off and most profound— who can discover it?

verses.textZh: 我转念，一心去了解、考察并寻觅智慧和事理，又要知道愚蒙是邪恶的，狂妄是愚昧的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我转念，一心去了解、考察并寻觅智慧和事理，又要知道愚蒙是邪恶的，狂妄是愚昧的。
verses.textZhCuv: 我转念，一心要知道，要考察，要寻求智慧和万事的理由；又要知道邪恶为愚昧，愚昧为狂妄。
verses.textEnNiv: So I turned my mind to understand, to investigate and to search out wisdom and the scheme of things and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the madness of folly.
verses.textEnEsv: I turned my heart to know and to search out and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know the wickedness of folly and the foolishness that is madness.
verses.textEnNkjv: I applied my heart to know, To search and seek out wisdom and the reason ofthings, To know the wickedness of folly, Even of foolishness and madness.
verses.textEnNlt: I searched everywhere, determined to find wisdom and to understand the reason for things. I was determined to prove to myself that wickedness is stupid and that foolishness is madness.
verses.textEnNasb: I directed my mind to know and to investigate, and to seek wisdom and an explanation, and to know the evil of foolishness and the foolishness of insanity.
verses.textEn: So I turned my mind to understand, to investigate and to search out wisdom and the scheme of things and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the madness of folly.

verses.textZh: 我发现一个比死亡更恶毒的妇人，她有如罗网，心如陷阱，手如锁炼。蒙神喜悦的人得以摆脱她，罪人却被她缠住。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我发现一个比死亡更恶毒的妇人，她有如罗网，心如陷阱，手如锁炼。蒙神喜悦的人得以摆脱她，罪人却被她缠住。
verses.textZhCuv: 我得知有等妇人比死还苦：她的心是网罗，手是锁链。凡蒙神喜悦的人必能躲避她；有罪的人却被她缠住了。
verses.textEnNiv: I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a trap and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner she will ensnare.
verses.textEnEsv: And I find something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and whose hands are fetters. He who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is taken by her.
verses.textEnNkjv: And I find more bitter than death The woman whose heart is snares and nets, Whose hands are fetters. He who pleases God shall escape from her, But the sinner shall be trapped by her.
verses.textEnNlt: I discovered that a seductive woman is a trap more bitter than death. Her passion is a snare, and her soft hands are chains. Those who are pleasing to God will escape her, but sinners will be caught in her snare.
verses.textEnNasb: And I discovered as more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. One who is pleasing to God will escape from her, but the sinner will be captured by her.
verses.textEn: I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a trap and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner she will ensnare.

verses.textZh: 传道者说："看哪！我发现了这件事，我一再揣摩，要找出事情的道理。
verses.textZhCnvs: 传道者说："看哪！我发现了这件事，我一再揣摩，要找出事情的道理。
verses.textZhCuv: 我所找到的只有一件，就是神造人原是正直，但他们寻出许多巧计。
verses.textEnNiv: "Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I have discovered: "Adding one thing to another to discover the scheme of things—
verses.textEnEsv: Behold, this is what I found, says the Preacher, while adding one thing to another to find the scheme of things—
verses.textEnNkjv: Here is what I have found," says the Preacher, "Adding one thing to the other to find out the reason,
verses.textEnNlt: "This is my conclusion," says the Teacher. "I discovered this after looking at the matter from every possible angle.
verses.textEnNasb: "Behold, I have discovered this," says the Preacher, "by adding one thing to another to find an explanation,
verses.textEn: "Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I have discovered: "Adding one thing to another to discover the scheme of things—

verses.textZh: 我的心仍在寻觅，却还找不到，就是在一千个男人中，我找到一个正直人，但在所有的女人中，连一个也找不到。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我的心仍在寻觅，却还找不到，就是在一千个男人中，我找到一个正直人，但在所有的女人中，连一个也找不到。
verses.textZhCuv: 我的心仍在寻觅，却还找不到，就是在一千个男人中，我找到一个正直人，但在所有的女人中，连一个也找不到。
verses.textEnNiv: while I was still searching but not finding— I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all.
verses.textEnEsv: which my soul has sought repeatedly, but I have not found. One man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
verses.textEnNkjv: Which my soul still seeks but I cannot find: One man among a thousand I have found, But a woman among all these I have not found.
verses.textEnNlt: Though I have searched repeatedly, I have not found what I was looking for. Only one out of a thousand men is virtuous, but not one woman!
verses.textEnNasb: which I am still seeking but have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all these.
verses.textEn: while I was still searching but not finding— I found one upright man among a thousand, but not one upright woman among them all.

verses.textZh: 我所明白的，只有这件事：神造人原是正直的，他们却找出许多巧计。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我所明白的，只有这件事：神造人原是正直的，他们却找出许多巧计。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我所明白的，只有这件事：神造人原是正直的，他们却找出许多巧计。"
verses.textEnNiv: This only have I found: God created mankind upright, but they have gone in search of many schemes."
verses.textEnEsv: See, this alone I found, that God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.
verses.textEnNkjv: Truly, this only I have found: That God made man upright, But they have sought out many schemes."
verses.textEnNlt: But I did find this: God created people to be virtuous, but they have each turned to follow their own downward path."
verses.textEnNasb: Behold, I have found only this, that God made people upright, but they have sought out many schemes."
verses.textEn: This only have I found: God created mankind upright, but they have gone in search of many schemes."

verses.textZh: 谁像智慧人，谁知道事情的解释呢？人的智慧使他容光焕发，使他脸上的戾气转消。
verses.textZhCnvs: 谁像智慧人，谁知道事情的解释呢？人的智慧使他容光焕发，使他脸上的戾气转消。
verses.textZhCuv: 谁如智慧人呢？ 谁知道事情的解释呢？ 人的智慧使他的脸发光， 并使他脸上的暴气改变。
verses.textEnNiv: Who is like the wise? Who knows the explanation of things? A person’s wisdom brightens their face and changes its hard appearance.
verses.textEnEsv: Who is like the wise? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
verses.textEnNkjv: Who is like a wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, And the sternness of his face is changed.
verses.textEnNlt: How wonderful to be wise, to analyze and interpret things. Wisdom lights up a person’s face, softening its harshness.
verses.textEnNasb: Who is like the wise person and who knows the meaning of a matter? A person’s wisdom illuminates his face and makes his stern face brighten up.
verses.textEn: Who is like the wise? Who knows the explanation of things? A person’s wisdom brightens their face and changes its hard appearance.

verses.textZh: 我劝你，因为你指着神起了誓，你就要遵守王的命令。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我劝你，因为你指着神起了誓，你就要遵守王的命令。
verses.textZhCuv: 我劝你遵守王的命令；既指神起誓，理当如此。
verses.textEnNiv: Obey the king’s command, I say, because you took an oath before God.
verses.textEnEsv: I say: Keep the king’s command, because of God’s oath to him.
verses.textEnNkjv: I say, "Keep the king’s commandment for the sake of your oath to God.
verses.textEnNlt: Obey the king since you vowed to God that you would.
verses.textEnNasb: I say, "Keep the command of the king because of the oath before God.
verses.textEn: Obey the king’s command, I say, because you took an oath before God.

verses.textZh: 不要轻率离开王的面前，也不要参与恶事，因为王可以随己意作任何事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 不要轻率离开王的面前，也不要参与恶事，因为王可以随己意作任何事。
verses.textZhCuv: 不要急躁离开王的面前，不要固执行恶，因为他凡事都随自己的心意而行。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not be in a hurry to leave the king’s presence. Do not stand up for a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
verses.textEnEsv: Be not hasty to go from his presence. Do not take your stand in an evil cause, for he does whatever he pleases.
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not be hasty to go from his presence. Do not take your stand for an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him."
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t try to avoid doing your duty, and don’t stand with those who plot evil, for the king can do whatever he wants.
verses.textEnNasb: Do not be in a hurry to leave him. Do not join in an evil matter, for he will do whatever he pleases."
verses.textEn: Do not be in a hurry to leave the king’s presence. Do not stand up for a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.

verses.textZh: 既然王的话有权柄，谁敢问他："你在作甚么？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 既然王的话有权柄，谁敢问他："你在作甚么？"
verses.textZhCuv: 王的话本有权力，谁敢问他说「你做什么」呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Since a king’s word is supreme, who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.textEnEsv: For the word of the king is supreme, and who may say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.textEnNkjv: Where the word of a king is, there is power; And who may say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.textEnNlt: His command is backed by great power. No one can resist or question it.
verses.textEnNasb: Since the word of the king is authoritative, who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.textEn: Since a king’s word is supreme, who can say to him, "What are you doing?"

verses.textZh: 遵守命令的，必不遭受灾祸；智慧人的心，晓得时机，懂得判断。
verses.textZhCnvs: 遵守命令的，必不遭受灾祸；智慧人的心，晓得时机，懂得判断。
verses.textZhCuv: 凡遵守命令的，必不经历祸患；智慧人的心能辨明时候和定理 。
verses.textEnNiv: Whoever obeys his command will come to no harm, and the wise heart will know the proper time and procedure.
verses.textEnEsv: Whoever keeps a command will know no evil thing, and the wise heart will know the proper time and the just way.
verses.textEnNkjv: He who keeps his command will experience nothing harmful; And a wise man’s heart discerns both time and judgment,
verses.textEnNlt: Those who obey him will not be punished. Those who are wise will find a time and a way to do what is right,
verses.textEnNasb: One who keeps a royal command experiences no trouble, for a wise heart knows the proper time and procedure.
verses.textEn: Whoever obeys his command will come to no harm, and the wise heart will know the proper time and procedure.

verses.textZh: 各样事务成就，都有合宜的时机和定局，尽管人的灾祸重压在自己身上。
verses.textZhCnvs: 各样事务成就，都有合宜的时机和定局，尽管人的灾祸重压在自己身上。
verses.textZhCuv: 各样事务成就都有时候和定理，因为人的苦难重压在他身上。
verses.textEnNiv: For there is a proper time and procedure for every matter, though a person may be weighed down by misery.
verses.textEnEsv: For there is a time and a way for everything, although man’s trouble lies heavy on him.
verses.textEnNkjv: Because for every matter there is a time and judgment, Though the misery of man increases greatly.
verses.textEnNlt: for there is a time and a way for everything, even when a person is in trouble.
verses.textEnNasb: For there is a proper time and procedure for every delight, though a person’s trouble is heavy upon him.
verses.textEn: For there is a proper time and procedure for every matter, though a person may be weighed down by misery.

verses.textZh: 他不晓得未来的事，将来要发生甚么，谁能告诉他呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 他不晓得未来的事，将来要发生甚么，谁能告诉他呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 他不知道将来的事，因为将来如何，谁能告诉他呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Since no one knows the future, who can tell someone else what is to come?
verses.textEnEsv: For he does not know what is to be, for who can tell him how it will be?
verses.textEnNkjv: For he does not know what will happen; So who can tell him when it will occur?
verses.textEnNlt: Indeed, how can people avoid what they don’t know is going to happen?
verses.textEnNasb: If no one knows what will happen, who can tell him when it will happen?
verses.textEn: Since no one knows the future, who can tell someone else what is to come?

verses.textZh: 没有人能支配风 ，把它留住；没有人能控制死期；战争之时，没有人能免役；邪恶救不了行邪恶的人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 没有人能支配风 ，把它留住；没有人能控制死期；战争之时，没有人能免役；邪恶救不了行邪恶的人。
verses.textZhCuv: 无人有权力掌管生命，将生命留住；也无人有权力掌管死期；这场争战，无人能免；邪恶也不能救那好行邪恶的人。
verses.textEnNiv: As no one has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has power over the time of their death. As no one is discharged in time of war, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
verses.textEnEsv: No man has power to retain the spirit, or power over the day of death. There is no discharge from war, nor will wickedness deliver those who are given to it.
verses.textEnNkjv: No one has power over the spirit to retain the spirit, And no one has power in the day of death. Thereis no release from that war, And wickedness will not deliver those who are given to it.
verses.textEnNlt: None of us can hold back our spirit from departing. None of us has the power to prevent the day of our death. There is no escaping that obligation, that dark battle. And in the face of death, wickedness will certainly not rescue the wicked.
verses.textEnNasb: No one has authority over the wind to restrain the wind, nor authority over the day of death; and there is no military discharge in the time of war, and evil will not save those who practice it.
verses.textEn: As no one has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has power over the time of their death. As no one is discharged in time of war, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.

verses.textZh: 我看见了这一切，又专心查究在日光之下所发生的一切事。有这样的一个时候：有人管辖别人，叫他受害。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我看见了这一切，又专心查究在日光之下所发生的一切事。有这样的一个时候：有人管辖别人，叫他受害。
verses.textZhCuv: 这一切我都见过，也专心查考日光之下所做的一切事。有时这人管辖那人，令人受害。
verses.textEnNiv: All this I saw, as I applied my mind to everything done under the sun. There is a time when a man lords it over others to his own hurt.
verses.textEnEsv: All this I observed while applying my heart to all that is done under the sun, when man had power over man to his hurt.
verses.textEnNkjv: All this I have seen, and applied my heart to every work that is done under the sun: Thereis a time in which one man rules over another to his own hurt.
verses.textEnNlt: I have thought deeply about all that goes on here under the sun, where people have the power to hurt each other.
verses.textEnNasb: All this I have seen, and have applied my mind to every deed that has been done under the sun at a time when one person has exercised authority over another person to his detriment.
verses.textEn: All this I saw, as I applied my mind to everything done under the sun. There is a time when a man lords it over others to his own hurt.

verses.textZh: 然后我看见恶人得以埋葬，他们生前在圣地往来，而在他们这样行的城中，竟被人遗忘。这也是虚空！
verses.textZhCnvs: 然后我看见恶人得以埋葬，他们生前在圣地往来，而在他们这样行的城中，竟被人遗忘。这也是虚空！
verses.textZhCuv: 我见恶人埋葬，归入坟墓；又见行正直事的离开圣地，在城中被人忘记。这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: Then too, I saw the wicked buried—those who used to come and go from the holy place and receive praise in the city where they did this. This too is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: Then I saw the wicked buried. They used to go in and out of the holy place and were praised in the city where they had done such things. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of holiness, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done. This also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: I have seen wicked people buried with honor. Yet they were the very ones who frequented the Temple and are now praised in the same city where they committed their crimes! This, too, is meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: So then, I have seen the wicked buried, those who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they are soon forgotten in the city where they did such things. This too is futility.
verses.textEn: Then too, I saw the wicked buried—those who used to come and go from the holy place and receive praise in the city where they did this. This too is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 对恶行已判定的刑罚迟迟没有执行，世人的心就充满行恶的意图。
verses.textZhCnvs: 对恶行已判定的刑罚迟迟没有执行，世人的心就充满行恶的意图。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为断定罪名不立刻施刑，所以世人满心作恶。
verses.textEnNiv: When the sentence for a crime is not quickly carried out, people’s hearts are filled with schemes to do wrong.
verses.textEnEsv: Because the sentence against an evil deed is not executed speedily, the heart of the children of man is fully set to do evil.
verses.textEnNkjv: Because the sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.textEnNlt: When a crime is not punished quickly, people feel it is safe to do wrong.
verses.textEnNasb: Because the sentence against an evil deed is not executed quickly, therefore the hearts of the sons of mankind among them are fully given to do evil.
verses.textEn: When the sentence for a crime is not quickly carried out, people’s hearts are filled with schemes to do wrong.

verses.textZh: 罪人既然作恶百次，还享长寿，那么我知道敬畏神的人，就是在他面前存敬畏的心的，必享福乐。
verses.textZhCnvs: 罪人既然作恶百次，还享长寿，那么我知道敬畏神的人，就是在他面前存敬畏的心的，必享福乐。
verses.textZhCuv: 罪人虽然作恶百次，倒享长久的年日；然而我准知道，敬畏神的，就是在他面前敬畏的人，终久必得福乐。
verses.textEnNiv: Although a wicked person who commits a hundred crimes may live a long time, I know that it will go better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.
verses.textEnEsv: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his life, yet I know that it will be well with those who fear God, because they fear before him.
verses.textEnNkjv: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him.
verses.textEnNlt: But even though a person sins a hundred times and still lives a long time, I know that those who fear God will be better off.
verses.textEnNasb: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and may lengthen his life, still I know that it will go well for those who fear God, who fear Him openly.
verses.textEn: Although a wicked person who commits a hundred crimes may live a long time, I know that it will go better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.

verses.textZh: 恶人却没有福乐，也得不到长寿；他好象影子的短暂，因为他在神面前不存敬畏的心。
verses.textZhCnvs: 恶人却没有福乐，也得不到长寿；他好象影子的短暂，因为他在神面前不存敬畏的心。
verses.textZhCuv: 恶人却不得福乐，也不得长久的年日；这年日好像影儿，因他不敬畏神。
verses.textEnNiv: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
verses.textEnEsv: But it will not be well with the wicked, neither will he prolong his days like a shadow, because he does not fear before God.
verses.textEnNkjv: But it will not be well with the wicked; nor will he prolong his days, whichare as a shadow, because he does not fear before God.
verses.textEnNlt: The wicked will not prosper, for they do not fear God. Their days will never grow long like the evening shadows.
verses.textEnNasb: But it will not go well for the evil person and he will not lengthen his days like a shadow, because he does not fear God.
verses.textEn: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.

verses.textZh: 在世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人照恶人所行的受报应，恶人照义人所行的得报偿。我说，这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人照恶人所行的受报应，恶人照义人所行的得报偿。我说，这也是虚空。
verses.textZhCuv: 世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人所遭遇的，反照恶人所行的；又有恶人所遭遇的，反照义人所行的。我说，这也是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: There is something else meaningless that occurs on earth: the righteous who get what the wicked deserve, and the wicked who get what the righteous deserve. This too, I say, is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: There is a vanity that takes place on earth, that there are righteous people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: There is a vanity which occurs on earth, that there are just men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: And this is not all that is meaningless in our world. In this life, good people are often treated as though they were wicked, and wicked people are often treated as though they were good. This is so meaningless!
verses.textEnNasb: There is futility which is done on the earth, that is, there are righteous people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the wicked. On the other hand, there are evil people to whom it happens according to the deeds of the righteous. I say that this too is futility.
verses.textEn: There is something else meaningless that occurs on earth: the righteous who get what the wicked deserve, and the wicked who get what the righteous deserve. This too, I say, is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 于是我称颂快乐，因为人在日光之下最好是吃喝快乐。这是人在日光之下，神赐给他一生的年日里，从自己劳碌中所得的享受。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我称颂快乐，因为人在日光之下最好是吃喝快乐。这是人在日光之下，神赐给他一生的年日里，从自己劳碌中所得的享受。
verses.textZhCuv: 我就称赞快乐，原来人在日光之下，莫强如吃喝快乐；因为他在日光之下，神赐他一生的年日，要从劳碌中，时常享受所得的。
verses.textEnNiv: So I commend the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad. Then joy will accompany them in their toil all the days of the life God has given them under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: And I commend joy, for man has nothing better under the sun but to eat and drink and be joyful, for this will go with him in his toil through the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: So I commended enjoyment, because a man has nothing better under the sun than to eat, drink, and be merry; for this will remain with him in his labor all the days of his life which God gives him under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: So I recommend having fun, because there is nothing better for people in this world than to eat, drink, and enjoy life. That way they will experience some happiness along with all the hard work God gives them under the sun.
verses.textEnNasb: So I commended pleasure, for there is nothing good for a person under the sun except to eat, drink, and be joyful, and this will stand by him in his labor throughout the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
verses.textEn: So I commend the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad. Then joy will accompany them in their toil all the days of the life God has given them under the sun.

verses.textZh: 我专心认识智慧，察看世上的劳碌─有人昼夜不眠─
verses.textZhCnvs: 我专心认识智慧，察看世上的劳碌─有人昼夜不眠─
verses.textZhCuv: 我专心求智慧，要看世上所做的事。（有昼夜不睡觉不合眼的。）
verses.textEnNiv: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the labor that is done on earth—people getting no sleep day or night—
verses.textEnEsv: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on earth, how neither day nor night do one’s eyes see sleep,
verses.textEnNkjv: When I applied my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on earth, even though one sees no sleep day or night,
verses.textEnNlt: In my search for wisdom and in my observation of people’s burdens here on earth, I discovered that there is ceaseless activity, day and night.
verses.textEnNasb: When I devoted my mind to know wisdom and to see the business which has been done on the earth (even though one should never sleep day or night),
verses.textEn: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the labor that is done on earth—people getting no sleep day or night—

verses.textZh: 于是我看见了神的一切作为，知道在日光之下所发生的事，人不能查明；尽管人劳碌寻查，总是查不出来；即使智慧人以为知道了，还是查不出来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我看见了神的一切作为，知道在日光之下所发生的事，人不能查明；尽管人劳碌寻查，总是查不出来；即使智慧人以为知道了，还是查不出来。
verses.textZhCuv: 我就看明神一切的作为，知道人查不出日光之下所做的事；任凭他费多少力寻查，都查不出来，就是智慧人虽想知道，也是查不出来。
verses.textEnNiv: then I saw all that God has done. No one can comprehend what goes on under the sun. Despite all their efforts to search it out, no one can discover its meaning. Even if the wise claim they know, they cannot really comprehend it.
verses.textEnEsv: then I saw all the work of God, that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. However much man may toil in seeking, he will not find it out. Even though a wise man claims to know, he cannot find it out.
verses.textEnNkjv: then I saw all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. For though a man labors to discover it, yet he will not find it; moreover, though a wise man attempts to know it, he will not be able to find it.
verses.textEnNlt: I realized that no one can discover everything God is doing under the sun. Not even the wisest people discover everything, no matter what they claim.
verses.textEnNasb: and I saw every work of God, I concluded that one cannot discover the work which has been done under the sun. Even though a person laboriously seeks, he will not discover; and even if the wise person claims to know, he cannot discover.
verses.textEn: then I saw all that God has done. No one can comprehend what goes on under the sun. Despite all their efforts to search it out, no one can discover its meaning. Even if the wise claim they know, they cannot really comprehend it.

verses.textZh: 我留心这一切事，并加以阐明：就是义人、智慧人和他们所作的，都在神手里。临到他们的一切，无论是爱是恨，人都不领悟。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我留心这一切事，并加以阐明：就是义人、智慧人和他们所作的，都在神手里。临到他们的一切，无论是爱是恨，人都不领悟。
verses.textZhCuv: 我将这一切事放在心上，详细考究，就知道义人和智慧人，并他们的作为都在神手中；或是爱，或是恨，都在他们的前面，人不能知道。
verses.textEnNiv: So I reflected on all this and concluded that the righteous and the wise and what they do are in God’s hands, but no one knows whether love or hate awaits them.
verses.textEnEsv: But all this I laid to heart, examining it all, how the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether it is love or hate, man does not know; both are before him.
verses.textEnNkjv: For I considered all this in my heart, so that I could declare it all: that the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God. People know neither love nor hatred by anything theysee before them.
verses.textEnNlt: This, too, I carefully explored: Even though the actions of godly and wise people are in God’s hands, no one knows whether God will show them favor.
verses.textEnNasb: For I have taken all this to my heart, even to examine it all, that righteous people, wise people, and their deeds are in the hand of God. People do not know whether it will be love or hatred; anything awaits them.
verses.textEn: So I reflected on all this and concluded that the righteous and the wise and what they do are in God’s hands, but no one knows whether love or hate awaits them.

verses.textZh: 众人的命运都是一样的：义人与恶人、好人与坏人、洁净的与不洁净的、献祭的与不献祭的，所遭遇的都是一样的；好人怎样，罪人也怎样；起誓的怎样，怕起誓的也怎样。
verses.textZhCnvs: 众人的命运都是一样的：义人与恶人、好人与坏人、洁净的与不洁净的、献祭的与不献祭的，所遭遇的都是一样的；好人怎样，罪人也怎样；起誓的怎样，怕起誓的也怎样。
verses.textZhCuv: 凡临到众人的事都是一样：义人和恶人都遭遇一样的事；好人，洁净人和不洁净人，献祭的与不献祭的，也是一样。好人如何，罪人也如何；起誓的如何，怕起誓的也如何。
verses.textEnNiv: All share a common destiny—the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good, so with the sinful; as it is with those who take oaths, so with those who are afraid to take them.
verses.textEnEsv: It is the same for all, since the same event happens to the righteous and the wicked, to the good and the evil, to the clean and the unclean, to him who sacrifices and him who does not sacrifice. As the good one is, so is the sinner, and he who swears is as he who shuns an oath.
verses.textEnNkjv: All things come alike to all: One event happens to the righteous and the wicked; To the good, the clean, and the unclean; To him who sacrifices and him who does not sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; He who takes an oath as he who fears an oath.
verses.textEnNlt: The same destiny ultimately awaits everyone, whether righteous or wicked, good or bad, ceremonially clean or unclean, religious or irreligious. Good people receive the same treatment as sinners, and people who make promises to God are treated like people who don’t.
verses.textEnNasb: It is the same for all. There is one fate for the righteous and for the wicked; for the good, for the clean and the unclean; for the person who offers a sacrifice and for the one who does not sacrifice. As the good person is, so is the sinner; the one who swears an oath is just as the one who is afraid to swear an oath.
verses.textEn: All share a common destiny—the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. As it is with the good, so with the sinful; as it is with those who take oaths, so with those who are afraid to take them.

verses.textZh: 在日光之下所发生的一切事，有一件令人遗憾的，就是众人的命运都是一样的，并且世人的心充满邪恶，一生心怀狂妄，后来都归到死人那里去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在日光之下所发生的一切事，有一件令人遗憾的，就是众人的命运都是一样的，并且世人的心充满邪恶，一生心怀狂妄，后来都归到死人那里去。
verses.textZhCuv: 在日光之下所行的一切事上有一件祸患，就是众人所遭遇的都是一样，并且世人的心充满了恶；活着的时候心里狂妄，后来就归死人那里去了。
verses.textEnNiv: This is the evil in everything that happens under the sun: The same destiny overtakes all. The hearts of people, moreover, are full of evil and there is madness in their hearts while they live, and afterward they join the dead.
verses.textEnEsv: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that the same event happens to all. Also, the hearts of the children of man are full of evil, and madness is in their hearts while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
