verses.textEnNkjv: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that one thing happens to all. Truly the hearts of the sons of men are full of evil; madness is in their hearts while they live, and after that theygo to the dead.
verses.textEnNlt: It seems so wrong that everyone under the sun suffers the same fate. Already twisted by evil, people choose their own mad course, for they have no hope. There is nothing ahead but death anyway.
verses.textEnNasb: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun, that there is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of the sons of mankind are full of evil, and insanity is in their hearts throughout their lives. Afterward they go to the dead.
verses.textEn: This is the evil in everything that happens under the sun: The same destiny overtakes all. The hearts of people, moreover, are full of evil and there is madness in their hearts while they live, and afterward they join the dead.

verses.textZh: 凡有生命的 ，就有盼望，因为活狗比死狮更好。
verses.textZhCnvs: 凡有生命的 ，就有盼望，因为活狗比死狮更好。
verses.textZhCuv: 与一切活人相连的，那人还有指望，因为活着的狗比死了的狮子更强。
verses.textEnNiv: Anyone who is among the living has hope —even a live dog is better off than a dead lion!
verses.textEnEsv: But he who is joined with all the living has hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.textEnNkjv: But for him who is joined to all the living there is hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.textEnNlt: There is hope only for the living. As they say, "It’s better to be a live dog than a dead lion!"
verses.textEnNasb: For whoever is joined to all the living, there is hope; for better a live dog, than a dead lion.
verses.textEn: Anyone who is among the living has hope —even a live dog is better off than a dead lion!

verses.textZh: 活人还知道自己必死，死人却一无所知，而且再得不到酬劳，他们也被遗忘。
verses.textZhCnvs: 活人还知道自己必死，死人却一无所知，而且再得不到酬劳，他们也被遗忘。
verses.textZhCuv: 活着的人知道必死；死了的人毫无所知，也不再得赏赐；他们的名无人记念。
verses.textEnNiv: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, and even their name is forgotten.
verses.textEnEsv: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing, and they have no more reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.textEnNkjv: For the living know that they will die; But the dead know nothing, And they have no more reward, For the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.textEnNlt: The living at least know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, nor are they remembered.
verses.textEnNasb: For the living know that they will die; but the dead do not know anything, nor do they have a reward any longer, for their memory is forgotten.
verses.textEn: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing; they have no further reward, and even their name is forgotten.

verses.textZh: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，都早已消失了，在日光之下所发生的一切事，永远也没有他们的分了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，都早已消失了，在日光之下所发生的一切事，永远也没有他们的分了。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，早都消灭了。在日光之下所行的一切事上，他们永不再有分了。
verses.textEnNiv: Their love, their hate and their jealousy have long since vanished; never again will they have a part in anything that happens under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: Their love and their hate and their envy have already perished, and forever they have no more share in all that is done under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy have now perished; Nevermore will they have a share In anything done under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: Whatever they did in their lifetime—loving, hating, envying—is all long gone. They no longer play a part in anything here on earth.
verses.textEnNasb: Indeed their love, their hate, and their zeal have already perished, and they will no longer have a share in all that is done under the sun.
verses.textEn: Their love, their hate and their jealousy have long since vanished; never again will they have a part in anything that happens under the sun.

verses.textZh: 你只管快快乐乐地去吃你的饭，怀着高兴的心去喝你的酒，因为神已经悦纳了你所作的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你只管快快乐乐地去吃你的饭，怀着高兴的心去喝你的酒，因为神已经悦纳了你所作的。
verses.textZhCuv: 你只管去欢欢喜喜吃你的饭，心中快乐喝你的酒，因为神已经悦纳你的作为。
verses.textEnNiv: Go, eat your food with gladness, and drink your wine with a joyful heart, for God has already approved what you do.
verses.textEnEsv: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart, for God has already approved what you do.
verses.textEnNkjv: Go, eat your bread with joy, And drink your wine with a merry heart; For God has already accepted your works.
verses.textEnNlt: So go ahead. Eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God approves of this!
verses.textEnNasb: Go then, eat your bread in happiness, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart; for God has already approved your works.
verses.textEn: Go, eat your food with gladness, and drink your wine with a joyful heart, for God has already approved what you do.

verses.textZh: 你当经常穿著白色的衣袍，头上也不要缺少膏油。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你当经常穿著白色的衣袍，头上也不要缺少膏油。
verses.textZhCuv: 你的衣服当时常洁白，你头上也不要缺少膏油。
verses.textEnNiv: Always be clothed in white, and always anoint your head with oil.
verses.textEnEsv: Let your garments be always white. Let not oil be lacking on your head.
verses.textEnNkjv: Let your garments always be white, And let your head lack no oil.
verses.textEnNlt: Wear fine clothes, with a splash of cologne!
verses.textEnNasb: See that your clothes are white all the time, and that there is no lack of oil on your head.
verses.textEn: Always be clothed in white, and always anoint your head with oil.

verses.textZh: 在你一生虚空的年日中，就是神在日光之下赐你虚空的年日中，你要和你所爱的妻子享受人生，因为那是你一生在日光之下从劳碌中所得的分。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在你一生虚空的年日中，就是神在日光之下赐你虚空的年日中，你要和你所爱的妻子享受人生，因为那是你一生在日光之下从劳碌中所得的分。
verses.textZhCuv: 在你一生虚空的年日，就是神赐你在日光之下虚空的年日，当同你所爱的妻，快活度日，因为那是你生前在日光之下劳碌的事上所得的分。
verses.textEnNiv: Enjoy life with your wife, whom you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun—all your meaningless days. For this is your lot in life and in your toilsome labor under the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: Enjoy life with the wife whom you love, all the days of your vain life that he has given you under the sun, because that is your portion in life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your vain life which He has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity; for that is your portion in life, and in the labor which you perform under the sun.
verses.textEnNlt: Live happily with the woman you love through all the meaningless days of life that God has given you under the sun. The wife God gives you is your reward for all your earthly toil.
verses.textEnNasb: Enjoy life with the wife whom you love all the days of your futile life which He has given you under the sun, all the days of your futility; for this is your reward in life and in your work which you have labored under the sun.
verses.textEn: Enjoy life with your wife, whom you love, all the days of this meaningless life that God has given you under the sun—all your meaningless days. For this is your lot in life and in your toilsome labor under the sun.

verses.textZh: 凡是你手可作的，都当尽力去作；因为在你所要去的阴间里，既没有工作，又没有筹谋；没有知识，也没有智慧。
verses.textZhCnvs: 凡是你手可作的，都当尽力去作；因为在你所要去的阴间里，既没有工作，又没有筹谋；没有知识，也没有智慧。
verses.textZhCuv: 凡你手所当做的事要尽力去做；因为在你所必去的阴间没有工作，没有谋算，没有知识，也没有智慧。
verses.textEnNiv: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in the realm of the dead, where you are going, there is neither working nor planning nor knowledge nor wisdom.
verses.textEnEsv: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might, for there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, to which you are going.
verses.textEnNkjv: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for thereis no work or device or knowledge or wisdom in the grave where you are going.
verses.textEnNlt: Whatever you do, do well. For when you go to the grave, there will be no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
verses.textEnNasb: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might; for there is no activity, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol where you are going.
verses.textEn: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might, for in the realm of the dead, where you are going, there is neither working nor planning nor knowledge nor wisdom.

verses.textZh: 我又看见在日光之下，跑得快的未必得奖，勇士未必战胜，智慧的未必得粮食，精明的未必致富，博学的未必得人赏识，因为时机和际遇左右众人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我又看见在日光之下，跑得快的未必得奖，勇士未必战胜，智慧的未必得粮食，精明的未必致富，博学的未必得人赏识，因为时机和际遇左右众人。
verses.textZhCuv: 我又转念：见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢；力战的未必得胜；智慧的未必得粮食；明哲的未必得资财；灵巧的未必得喜悦。所临到众人的是在乎当时的机会。
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift or the battle to the strong, nor does food come to the wise or wealth to the brilliant or favor to the learned; but time and chance happen to them all.
verses.textEnEsv: Again I saw that under the sun the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the intelligent, nor favor to those with knowledge, but time and chance happen to them all.
verses.textEnNkjv: I returned and saw under the sun that— The race is not to the swift, Nor the battle to the strong, Nor bread to the wise, Nor riches to men of understanding, Nor favor to men of skill; But time and chance happen to them all.
verses.textEnNlt: I have observed something else under the sun. The fastest runner doesn’t always win the race, and the strongest warrior doesn’t always win the battle. The wise sometimes go hungry, and the skillful are not necessarily wealthy. And those who are educated don’t always lead successful lives. It is all decided by chance, by being in the right place at the right time.
verses.textEnNasb: I again saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift and the battle is not to the warriors, and neither is bread to the wise nor wealth to the discerning, nor favor to the skillful; for time and chance overtake them all.
verses.textEn: I have seen something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift or the battle to the strong, nor does food come to the wise or wealth to the brilliant or favor to the learned; but time and chance happen to them all.

verses.textZh: 原来人并不知道自己的时机，正像鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，险恶的时机忽然临到世人身上的时候，世人也照样陷在其中。
verses.textZhCnvs: 原来人并不知道自己的时机，正像鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，险恶的时机忽然临到世人身上的时候，世人也照样陷在其中。
verses.textZhCuv: 原来人也不知道自己的定期。鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，祸患忽然临到的时候，世人陷在其中也是如此。
verses.textEnNiv: Moreover, no one knows when their hour will come: As fish are caught in a cruel net, or birds are taken in a snare, so people are trapped by evil times that fall unexpectedly upon them.
verses.textEnEsv: For man does not know his time. Like fish that are taken in an evil net, and like birds that are caught in a snare, so the children of man are snared at an evil time, when it suddenly falls upon them.
verses.textEnNkjv: For man also does not know his time: Like fish taken in a cruel net, Like birds caught in a snare, So the sons of men are snared in an evil time, When it falls suddenly upon them.
verses.textEnNlt: People can never predict when hard times might come. Like fish in a net or birds in a trap, people are caught by sudden tragedy.
verses.textEnNasb: For indeed, a person does not know his time: like fish that are caught in a treacherous net and birds caught in a snare, so the sons of mankind are ensnared at an evil time when it suddenly falls on them.
verses.textEn: Moreover, no one knows when their hour will come: As fish are caught in a cruel net, or birds are taken in a snare, so people are trapped by evil times that fall unexpectedly upon them.

verses.textZh: 在日光之下，我又看见一样智慧，觉得很有意义：
verses.textZhCnvs: 在日光之下，我又看见一样智慧，觉得很有意义：
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下有一样智慧，据我看乃是广大，
verses.textEnNiv: I also saw under the sun this example of wisdom that greatly impressed me:
verses.textEnEsv: I have also seen this example of wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me.
verses.textEnNkjv: This wisdom I have also seen under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
verses.textEnNlt: Here is another bit of wisdom that has impressed me as I have watched the way our world works.
verses.textEnNasb: This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it impressed me:
verses.textEn: I also saw under the sun this example of wisdom that greatly impressed me:

verses.textZh: 有一座小城，人数不多；有一个大君王来进攻，把它包围，建造巨大的高垒攻城。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有一座小城，人数不多；有一个大君王来进攻，把它包围，建造巨大的高垒攻城。
verses.textZhCuv: 就是有一小城，其中的人数稀少，有大君王来攻击，修筑营垒，将城围困。
verses.textEnNiv: There was once a small city with only a few people in it. And a powerful king came against it, surrounded it and built huge siege works against it.
verses.textEnEsv: There was a little city with few men in it, and a great king came against it and besieged it, building great siegeworks against it.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therewas a little city with few men in it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great snares around it.
verses.textEnNlt: There was a small town with only a few people, and a great king came with his army and besieged it.
verses.textEnNasb: there was a small city with few men in it, and a great king came to it, surrounded it, and constructed large siegeworks against it.
verses.textEn: There was once a small city with only a few people in it. And a powerful king came against it, surrounded it and built huge siege works against it.

verses.textZh: 城里有一个贫穷但有智慧的人，用他的智慧救了那城。然而，却没有人记念那穷人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 城里有一个贫穷但有智慧的人，用他的智慧救了那城。然而，却没有人记念那穷人。
verses.textZhCuv: 城中有一个贫穷的智慧人，他用智慧救了那城，却没有人记念那穷人。
verses.textEnNiv: Now there lived in that city a man poor but wise, and he saved the city by his wisdom. But nobody remembered that poor man.
verses.textEnEsv: But there was found in it a poor, wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city. Yet no one remembered that same poor man.
verses.textEnNlt: A poor, wise man knew how to save the town, and so it was rescued. But afterward no one thought to thank him.
verses.textEnNasb: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
verses.textEn: Now there lived in that city a man poor but wise, and he saved the city by his wisdom. But nobody remembered that poor man.

verses.textZh: 于是我说："智慧胜过武力"，但是那个穷人的智慧被藐视，他的话也没有人听从。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是我说："智慧胜过武力"，但是那个穷人的智慧被藐视，他的话也没有人听从。
verses.textZhCuv: 我就说，智慧胜过勇力；然而那贫穷人的智慧被人藐视，他的话也无人听从。
verses.textEnNiv: So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are no longer heeded.
verses.textEnEsv: But I say that wisdom is better than might, though the poor man’s wisdom is despised and his words are not heard.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then I said: "Wisdom is better than strength. Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, And his words are not heard.
verses.textEnNlt: So even though wisdom is better than strength, those who are wise will be despised if they are poor. What they say will not be appreciated for long.
verses.textEnNasb: So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are ignored.
verses.textEn: So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength." But the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are no longer heeded.

verses.textZh: 听智慧人安安静静说出来的话，胜过听管理愚昧者的人的喊叫。
verses.textZhCnvs: 听智慧人安安静静说出来的话，胜过听管理愚昧者的人的喊叫。
verses.textZhCuv: 宁可在安静之中听智慧人的言语，不听掌管愚昧人的喊声。
verses.textEnNiv: The quiet words of the wise are more to be heeded than the shouts of a ruler of fools.
verses.textEnEsv: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
verses.textEnNkjv: Words of the wise, spoken quietly, shouldbe heard Rather than the shout of a ruler of fools.
verses.textEnNlt: Better to hear the quiet words of a wise person than the shouts of a foolish king.
verses.textEnNasb: The words of the wise heard in calm are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
verses.textEn: The quiet words of the wise are more to be heeded than the shouts of a ruler of fools.

verses.textZh: 智慧胜于战斗的武器，但一个罪人能破坏许多好事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧胜于战斗的武器，但一个罪人能破坏许多好事。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧胜过打仗的兵器；但一个罪人能败坏许多善事。
verses.textEnNiv: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.textEnEsv: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.textEnNkjv: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; But one sinner destroys much good."
verses.textEnNlt: Better to have wisdom than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much that is good.
verses.textEnNasb: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.textEn: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

verses.textZh: 几只死苍蝇能使做香料者的膏油发霉变臭，一点点愚昧比智慧和荣誉的影响更大。
verses.textZhCnvs: 几只死苍蝇能使做香料者的膏油发霉变臭，一点点愚昧比智慧和荣誉的影响更大。
verses.textZhCuv: 死苍蝇使做香的膏油发出臭气； 这样，一点愚昧也能败坏智慧和尊荣。
verses.textEnNiv: As dead flies give perfume a bad smell, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
verses.textEnEsv: Dead flies make the perfumer’s ointment give off a stench; so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
verses.textEnNkjv: Dead flies putrefy the perfumer’s ointment, And cause it to give off a foul odor; Sodoes a little folly to one respected for wisdom and honor.
verses.textEnNlt: As dead flies cause even a bottle of perfume to stink, so a little foolishness spoils great wisdom and honor.
verses.textEnNasb: Dead flies turn a perfumer’s oil rancid, so a little foolishness is more potent than wisdom and honor.
verses.textEn: As dead flies give perfume a bad smell, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

verses.textZh: 智慧人的心向右，愚昧人的心偏左。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人的心向右，愚昧人的心偏左。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人的心居右； 愚昧人的心居左。
verses.textEnNiv: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool to the left.
verses.textEnEsv: A wise man’s heart inclines him to the right, but a fool’s heart to the left.
verses.textEnNkjv: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, But a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.textEnNlt: A wise person chooses the right road; a fool takes the wrong one.
verses.textEnNasb: A wise person’s heart directs him toward the right, but the foolish person’s heart directs him toward the left.
verses.textEn: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool to the left.

verses.textZh: 愚昧人连走路的时候，也显出无知；他对每一个人表现出他是个愚昧人 。
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人连走路的时候，也显出无知；他对每一个人表现出他是个愚昧人 。
verses.textZhCuv: 并且愚昧人行路显出无知， 对众人说，他是愚昧人。
verses.textEnNiv: Even as fools walk along the road, they lack sense and show everyone how stupid they are.
verses.textEnEsv: Even when the fool walks on the road, he lacks sense, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
verses.textEnNkjv: Even when a fool walks along the way, He lacks wisdom, And he shows everyone that he is a fool.
verses.textEnNlt: You can identify fools just by the way they walk down the street!
verses.textEnNasb: Even when the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he demonstrates to everyone that he is a fool.
verses.textEn: Even as fools walk along the road, they lack sense and show everyone how stupid they are.

verses.textZh: 如果掌权者向你发怒，你不要离开原位，因为柔顺能免大过。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果掌权者向你发怒，你不要离开原位，因为柔顺能免大过。
verses.textZhCuv: 掌权者的心若向你发怒， 不要离开你的本位， 因为柔和能免大过。
verses.textEnNiv: If a ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your post; calmness can lay great offenses to rest.
verses.textEnEsv: If the anger of the ruler rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness will lay great offenses to rest.
verses.textEnNkjv: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, Do not leave your post; For conciliation pacifies great offenses.
verses.textEnNlt: If your boss is angry at you, don’t quit! A quiet spirit can overcome even great mistakes.
verses.textEnNasb: If the ruler’s temper rises against you, do not abandon your place, because composure puts great offenses to rest.
verses.textEn: If a ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your post; calmness can lay great offenses to rest.

verses.textZh: 在日光之下我看见一件憾事，好象是出于官长无意的错误，
verses.textZhCnvs: 在日光之下我看见一件憾事，好象是出于官长无意的错误，
verses.textZhCuv: 我见日光之下有一件祸患， 似乎出于掌权的错误，
verses.textEnNiv: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the sort of error that arises from a ruler:
verses.textEnEsv: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as it were an error proceeding from the ruler:
verses.textEnNkjv: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, As an error proceeding from the ruler:
verses.textEnNlt: There is another evil I have seen under the sun. Kings and rulers make a grave mistake
verses.textEnNasb: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like a mistake that proceeds from the ruler:
verses.textEn: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the sort of error that arises from a ruler:

verses.textZh: 就是愚昧人得居众多高位，富有的人却处卑位。
verses.textZhCnvs: 就是愚昧人得居众多高位，富有的人却处卑位。
verses.textZhCuv: 就是愚昧人立在高位； 富足人坐在低位。
verses.textEnNiv: Fools are put in many high positions, while the rich occupy the low ones.
verses.textEnEsv: folly is set in many high places, and the rich sit in a low place.
verses.textEnNkjv: Folly is set in great dignity, While the rich sit in a lowly place.
verses.textEnNlt: when they give great authority to foolish people and low positions to people of proven worth.
verses.textEnNasb: foolishness is set in many exalted places while the rich sit in humble places.
verses.textEn: Fools are put in many high positions, while the rich occupy the low ones.

verses.textZh: 我见过奴仆骑马，贵族却像奴仆一样在地上步行。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我见过奴仆骑马，贵族却像奴仆一样在地上步行。
verses.textZhCuv: 我见过仆人骑马， 王子像仆人在地上步行。
verses.textEnNiv: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
verses.textEnEsv: I have seen slaves on horses, and princes walking on the ground like slaves.
verses.textEnNkjv: I have seen servants on horses, While princes walk on the ground like servants.
verses.textEnNlt: I have even seen servants riding horseback like princes—and princes walking like servants!
verses.textEnNasb: I have seen slaves riding on horses and princes walking like slaves on the land.
verses.textEn: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.

verses.textZh: 挖陷阱的，自己掉进去；拆墙垣的，有蛇来咬他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 挖陷阱的，自己掉进去；拆墙垣的，有蛇来咬他。
verses.textZhCuv: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中； 拆墙垣的，必为蛇所咬。
verses.textEnNiv: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
verses.textEnEsv: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and a serpent will bite him who breaks through a wall.
verses.textEnNkjv: He who digs a pit will fall into it, And whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a serpent.
verses.textEnNlt: When you dig a well, you might fall in. When you demolish an old wall, you could be bitten by a snake.
verses.textEnNasb: One who digs a pit may fall into it, and a serpent may bite one who breaks through a wall.
verses.textEn: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

verses.textZh: 采石的，被石打伤；劈柴的，被柴损害。
verses.textZhCnvs: 采石的，被石打伤；劈柴的，被柴损害。
verses.textZhCuv: 凿开 石头的，必受损伤； 劈开木头的，必遭危险。
verses.textEnNiv: Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them; whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.
verses.textEnEsv: He who quarries stones is hurt by them, and he who splits logs is endangered by them.
verses.textEnNkjv: He who quarries stones may be hurt by them, And he who splits wood may be endangered by it.
verses.textEnNlt: When you work in a quarry, stones might fall and crush you. When you chop wood, there is danger with each stroke of your ax.
verses.textEnNasb: One who quarries stones may be hurt by them, and one who splits logs may be endangered by them.
verses.textEn: Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them; whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.

verses.textZh: 斧头若钝了，还不把斧刃磨快，就必多费力气；智慧的好处在于助人成功。
verses.textZhCnvs: 斧头若钝了，还不把斧刃磨快，就必多费力气；智慧的好处在于助人成功。
verses.textZhCuv: 铁器钝了，若不将刃磨快，就必多费气力； 但得智慧指教，便有益处。
verses.textEnNiv: If the ax is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength is needed, but skill will bring success.
verses.textEnEsv: If the iron is blunt, and one does not sharpen the edge, he must use more strength, but wisdom helps one to succeed.
verses.textEnNkjv: If the ax is dull, And one does not sharpen the edge, Then he must use more strength; But wisdom brings success.
verses.textEnNlt: Using a dull ax requires great strength, so sharpen the blade. That’s the value of wisdom; it helps you succeed.
verses.textEnNasb: If the axe is dull and he does not sharpen its edge, then he must exert more strength. Wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.
verses.textEn: If the ax is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength is needed, but skill will bring success.

verses.textZh: 未行法术先被蛇咬，那么，法术对行法术的人就毫无用处。
verses.textZhCnvs: 未行法术先被蛇咬，那么，法术对行法术的人就毫无用处。
verses.textZhCuv: 未行法术以先，蛇若咬人， 后行法术也是无益。
verses.textEnNiv: If a snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer receives no fee.
verses.textEnEsv: If the serpent bites before it is charmed, there is no advantage to the charmer.
verses.textEnNkjv: A serpent may bite when itis not charmed; The babbler is no different.
verses.textEnNlt: If a snake bites before you charm it, what’s the use of being a snake charmer?
verses.textEnNasb: If the serpent bites before being charmed, there is no benefit for the charmer.
verses.textEn: If a snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer receives no fee.

verses.textZh: 智慧人的口，说出恩言；愚昧人的嘴，却吞灭自己。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人的口，说出恩言；愚昧人的嘴，却吞灭自己。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人的口说出恩言； 愚昧人的嘴吞灭自己。
verses.textEnNiv: Words from the mouth of the wise are gracious, but fools are consumed by their own lips.
verses.textEnEsv: The words of a wise man’s mouth win him favor, but the lips of a fool consume him.
verses.textEnNkjv: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, But the lips of a fool shall swallow him up;
verses.textEnNlt: Wise words bring approval, but fools are destroyed by their own words.
verses.textEnNasb: Words from the mouth of a wise person are gracious, while the lips of a fool consume him;
verses.textEn: Words from the mouth of the wise are gracious, but fools are consumed by their own lips.

verses.textZh: 愚昧人的话开头是愚昧，结尾是邪恶狂妄。
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人的话开头是愚昧，结尾是邪恶狂妄。
verses.textZhCuv: 他口中的言语起头是愚昧； 他话的末尾是奸恶的狂妄。
verses.textEnNiv: At the beginning their words are folly; at the end they are wicked madness—
verses.textEnEsv: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness, and the end of his talk is evil madness.
verses.textEnNkjv: The words of his mouth begin with foolishness, And the end of his talk is raving madness.
verses.textEnNlt: Fools base their thoughts on foolish assumptions, so their conclusions will be wicked madness;
verses.textEnNasb: the beginning of his talking is foolishness, and the end of it is evil insanity.
verses.textEn: At the beginning their words are folly; at the end they are wicked madness—

verses.textZh: 愚昧人多言多语。人不知道将来会有甚么事，谁能告诉他死后会发生甚么事呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人多言多语。人不知道将来会有甚么事，谁能告诉他死后会发生甚么事呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 愚昧人多有言语， 人却不知将来有什么事； 他身后的事谁能告诉他呢？
verses.textEnNiv: and fools multiply words. No one knows what is coming— who can tell someone else what will happen after them?
verses.textEnEsv: A fool multiplies words, though no man knows what is to be, and who can tell him what will be after him?
verses.textEnNkjv: A fool also multiplies words. No man knows what is to be; Who can tell him what will be after him?
verses.textEnNlt: they chatter on and on. No one really knows what is going to happen; no one can predict the future.
verses.textEnNasb: Yet the fool multiplies words. No person knows what will happen, and who can tell him what will come after him?
verses.textEn: and fools multiply words. No one knows what is coming— who can tell someone else what will happen after them?

verses.textZh: 愚昧人的劳碌徒使自己困乏，他连怎样进城也不知道。
verses.textZhCnvs: 愚昧人的劳碌徒使自己困乏，他连怎样进城也不知道。
verses.textZhCuv: 凡愚昧人，他的劳碌使自己困乏， 因为连进城的路，他也不知道。
verses.textEnNiv: The toil of fools wearies them; they do not know the way to town.
verses.textEnEsv: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
verses.textEnNkjv: The labor of fools wearies them, For they do not even know how to go to the city!
verses.textEnNlt: Fools are so exhausted by a little work that they can’t even find their way home.
verses.textEnNasb: The labor of a fool makes him so weary that he does not even know how to go to a city.
verses.textEn: The toil of fools wearies them; they do not know the way to town.

verses.textZh: 邦国啊，如果你的王是个孩童，而你的大臣又一早吃喝宴乐，你就有祸了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 邦国啊，如果你的王是个孩童，而你的大臣又一早吃喝宴乐，你就有祸了。
verses.textZhCuv: 邦国啊，你的王若是孩童， 你的群臣早晨宴乐， 你就有祸了！
verses.textEnNiv: Woe to the land whose king was a servant and whose princes feast in the morning.
verses.textEnEsv: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, and your princes feast in the morning!
verses.textEnNkjv: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, And your princes feast in the morning!
verses.textEnNlt: What sorrow for the land ruled by a servant, the land whose leaders feast in the morning.
verses.textEnNasb: Woe to you, land whose king is a boy, and whose princes feast in the morning.
verses.textEn: Woe to the land whose king was a servant and whose princes feast in the morning.

verses.textZh: 邦国啊，如果你的王是贵冑之子，而你的大臣又按时吃喝，为要得力，不为醉酒，你就有福了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 邦国啊，如果你的王是贵冑之子，而你的大臣又按时吃喝，为要得力，不为醉酒，你就有福了。
verses.textZhCuv: 邦国啊，你的王若是贵胄之子， 你的群臣按时吃喝， 为要补力，不为酒醉， 你就有福了！
verses.textEnNiv: Blessed is the land whose king is of noble birth and whose princes eat at a proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.
verses.textEnEsv: Happy are you, O land, when your king is the son of the nobility, and your princes feast at the proper time, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.textEnNkjv: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, And your princes feast at the proper time— For strength and not for drunkenness!
verses.textEnNlt: Happy is the land whose king is a noble leader and whose leaders feast at the proper time to gain strength for their work, not to get drunk.
verses.textEnNasb: Blessed are you, land whose king is of nobility, and whose princes eat at the appropriate time—for strength and not for drunkenness.
verses.textEn: Blessed is the land whose king is of noble birth and whose princes eat at a proper time— for strength and not for drunkenness.

verses.textZh: 房顶塌下是因为懒惰，房屋滴漏是因为懒得动手。
verses.textZhCnvs: 房顶塌下是因为懒惰，房屋滴漏是因为懒得动手。
verses.textZhCuv: 因人懒惰，房顶塌下； 因人手懒，房屋滴漏。
verses.textEnNiv: Through laziness, the rafters sag; because of idle hands, the house leaks.
verses.textEnEsv: Through sloth the roof sinks in, and through indolence the house leaks.
verses.textEnNkjv: Because of laziness the building decays, And through idleness of hands the house leaks.
verses.textEnNlt: Laziness leads to a sagging roof; idleness leads to a leaky house.
verses.textEnNasb: Through extreme laziness the rafters sag, and through idleness the house leaks.
verses.textEn: Through laziness, the rafters sag; because of idle hands, the house leaks.

verses.textZh: 设宴是为欢笑，酒能使人生快活，金钱能解决万事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 设宴是为欢笑，酒能使人生快活，金钱能解决万事。
verses.textZhCuv: 设摆筵席是为喜笑。 酒能使人快活； 钱能叫万事应心。
verses.textEnNiv: A feast is made for laughter, wine makes life merry, and money is the answer for everything.
verses.textEnEsv: Bread is made for laughter, and wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.
verses.textEnNkjv: A feast is made for laughter, And wine makes merry; But money answers everything.
verses.textEnNlt: A party gives laughter, wine gives happiness, and money gives everything!
verses.textEnNasb: People prepare a meal for enjoyment, wine makes life joyful, and money is the answer to everything.
verses.textEn: A feast is made for laughter, wine makes life merry, and money is the answer for everything.

verses.textZh: 不要在意念中咒骂君王，也不要在卧房中咒骂财主，因为空中的飞鸟会传声，有翅膀的会述说这事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 不要在意念中咒骂君王，也不要在卧房中咒骂财主，因为空中的飞鸟会传声，有翅膀的会述说这事。
verses.textZhCuv: 你不可咒诅君王， 也不可心怀此念； 在你卧房也不可咒诅富户。 因为空中的鸟必传扬这声音， 有翅膀的也必述说这事。
verses.textEnNiv: Do not revile the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird in the sky may carry your words, and a bird on the wing may report what you say.
verses.textEnEsv: Even in your thoughts, do not curse the king, nor in your bedroom curse the rich, for a bird of the air will carry your voice, or some winged creature tell the matter.
verses.textEnNkjv: Do not curse the king, even in your thought; Do not curse the rich, even in your bedroom; For a bird of the air may carry your voice, And a bird in flight may tell the matter.
verses.textEnNlt: Never make light of the king, even in your thoughts. And don’t make fun of the powerful, even in your own bedroom. For a little bird might deliver your message and tell them what you said.
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, in your bedroom do not curse a king, and in your sleeping rooms do not curse a rich person; for a bird of the sky will bring the sound, and the winged one will make your word known.
verses.textEn: Do not revile the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird in the sky may carry your words, and a bird on the wing may report what you say.

verses.textZh: 要把你的粮食撒在水面上，因为日久你必得回。
verses.textZhCnvs: 要把你的粮食撒在水面上，因为日久你必得回。
verses.textZhCuv: 当将你的粮食撒在水面， 因为日久必能得着。
verses.textEnNiv: Ship your grain across the sea; after many days you may receive a return.
verses.textEnEsv: Cast your bread upon the waters, for you will find it after many days.
verses.textEnNkjv: Cast your bread upon the waters, For you will find it after many days.
verses.textEnNlt: Send your grain across the seas, and in time, profits will flow back to you.
verses.textEnNasb: Cast your bread on the surface of the waters, for you will find it after many days.
verses.textEn: Ship your grain across the sea; after many days you may receive a return.

verses.textZh: 你要分为七份，或分为八份，因为你不知道将来会有甚么灾祸在地上发生。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你要分为七份，或分为八份，因为你不知道将来会有甚么灾祸在地上发生。
verses.textZhCuv: 你要分给七人，或分给八人， 因为你不知道将来有什么灾祸临到地上。
verses.textEnNiv: Invest in seven ventures, yes, in eight; you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.
verses.textEnEsv: Give a portion to seven, or even to eight, for you know not what disaster may happen on earth.
verses.textEnNkjv: Give a serving to seven, and also to eight, For you do not know what evil will be on the earth.
verses.textEnNlt: But divide your investments among many places, for you do not know what risks might lie ahead.
verses.textEnNasb: Divide your portion to seven, or even to eight, for you do not know what misfortune may occur on the earth.
verses.textEn: Invest in seven ventures, yes, in eight; you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.

verses.textZh: 云若充满水气，雨就倾倒在地上；树无论向南倒，或向北倒，倒在哪里，就横在哪里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 云若充满水气，雨就倾倒在地上；树无论向南倒，或向北倒，倒在哪里，就横在哪里。
verses.textZhCuv: 云若满了雨，就必倾倒在地上。 树若向南倒，或向北倒， 树倒在何处，就存在何处。
verses.textEnNiv: If clouds are full of water, they pour rain on the earth. Whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
verses.textEnEsv: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth, and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will lie.
verses.textEnNkjv: If the clouds are full of rain, They empty themselves upon the earth; And if a tree falls to the south or the north, In the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.
verses.textEnNlt: When clouds are heavy, the rains come down. Whether a tree falls north or south, it stays where it falls.
verses.textEnNasb: If the clouds are full, they pour out rain on the earth; and whether a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, wherever the tree falls, there it lies.
verses.textEn: If clouds are full of water, they pour rain on the earth. Whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

verses.textZh: 看风的，不撒种；观云的，不收割。
verses.textZhCnvs: 看风的，不撒种；观云的，不收割。
verses.textZhCuv: 看风的，必不撒种； 望云的，必不收割。
verses.textEnNiv: Whoever watches the wind will not plant; whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.
verses.textEnEsv: He who observes the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap.
verses.textEnNkjv: He who observes the wind will not sow, And he who regards the clouds will not reap.
verses.textEnNlt: Farmers who wait for perfect weather never plant. If they watch every cloud, they never harvest.
verses.textEnNasb: One who watches the wind will not sow and one who looks at the clouds will not harvest.
verses.textEn: Whoever watches the wind will not plant; whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.

verses.textZh: 你不晓得风的路向，不知道骨头如何在孕妇胎中形成，照样，创造万物之神的作为，你也不得而知。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你不晓得风的路向，不知道骨头如何在孕妇胎中形成，照样，创造万物之神的作为，你也不得而知。
verses.textZhCuv: 风从何道来，骨头在怀孕妇人的胎中如何长成，你尚且不得知道；这样，行万事之神的作为，你更不得知道。
verses.textEnNiv: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the body is formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
verses.textEnEsv: As you do not know the way the spirit comes to the bones in the womb of a woman with child, so you do not know the work of God who makes everything.
verses.textEnNkjv: As you do not know what is the way of the wind, Or how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, So you do not know the works of God who makes everything.
verses.textEnNlt: Just as you cannot understand the path of the wind or the mystery of a tiny baby growing in its mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the activity of God, who does all things.
verses.textEnNasb: Just as you do not know the path of the wind, and how bones are formed in the womb of the pregnant woman, so you do not know the activity of God who makes everything.
verses.textEn: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the body is formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

verses.textZh: 早晨要撒你的种，直到黄昏也不要歇手；因为你不知道哪一样种得成，是早撒的，或晚撒的，或两者都一样好。
verses.textZhCnvs: 早晨要撒你的种，直到黄昏也不要歇手；因为你不知道哪一样种得成，是早撒的，或晚撒的，或两者都一样好。
verses.textZhCuv: 早晨要撒你的种，晚上也不要歇你的手，因为你不知道哪一样发旺；或是早撒的，或是晚撒的，或是两样都好。
verses.textEnNiv: Sow your seed in the morning, and at evening let your hands not be idle, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both will do equally well.
verses.textEnEsv: In the morning sow your seed, and at evening withhold not your hand, for you do not know which will prosper, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
verses.textEnNkjv: In the morning sow your seed, And in the evening do not withhold your hand; For you do not know which will prosper, Either this or that, Or whether both alike willbe good.
verses.textEnNlt: Plant your seed in the morning and keep busy all afternoon, for you don’t know if profit will come from one activity or another—or maybe both.
verses.textEnNasb: Sow your seed in the morning and do not be idle in the evening, for you do not know whether one or the other will succeed, or whether both of them alike will be good.
verses.textEn: Sow your seed in the morning, and at evening let your hands not be idle, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both will do equally well.

verses.textZh: 光是美好的，眼睛得见天日，也是好的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 光是美好的，眼睛得见天日，也是好的。
verses.textZhCuv: 光本是佳美的，眼见日光也是可悦的。
verses.textEnNiv: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
verses.textEnEsv: Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.textEnNkjv: Truly the light is sweet, And itis pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun;
verses.textEnNlt: Light is sweet; how pleasant to see a new day dawning.
verses.textEnNasb: The light is pleasant, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.textEn: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

verses.textZh: 人无论多长寿，都当乐在其中，不过他要想到黑暗的日子，因为这些日子将会很多；要来的，都是虚空的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人无论多长寿，都当乐在其中，不过他要想到黑暗的日子，因为这些日子将会很多；要来的，都是虚空的。
verses.textZhCuv: 人活多年，就当快乐多年；然而也当想到黑暗的日子。因为这日子必多，所要来的都是虚空。
verses.textEnNiv: However many years anyone may live, let them enjoy them all. But let them remember the days of darkness, for there will be many. Everything to come is meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: So if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember that the days of darkness will be many. All that comes is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: But if a man lives many years And rejoices in them all, Yet let him remember the days of darkness, For they will be many. All that is coming is vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: When people live to be very old, let them rejoice in every day of life. But let them also remember there will be many dark days. Everything still to come is meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: Indeed, if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything that is to come will be futility.
verses.textEn: However many years anyone may live, let them enjoy them all. But let them remember the days of darkness, for there will be many. Everything to come is meaningless.

verses.textZh: 年轻人哪！你在幼年时要快乐，在壮年的日子，要使你的心欢畅；顺着你心所愿的，眼所见的去行。不过，你要知道，为了这一切事，神必审问你。
verses.textZhCnvs: 年轻人哪！你在幼年时要快乐，在壮年的日子，要使你的心欢畅；顺着你心所愿的，眼所见的去行。不过，你要知道，为了这一切事，神必审问你。
verses.textZhCuv: 少年人哪，你在幼年时当快乐。在幼年的日子，使你的心欢畅，行你心所愿行的，看你眼所爱看的；却要知道，为这一切的事，神必审问你。
verses.textEnNiv: You who are young, be happy while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Follow the ways of your heart and whatever your eyes see, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.textEnEsv: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes. But know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.textEnNkjv: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, And let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth; Walk in the ways of your heart, And in the sight of your eyes; But know that for all these God will bring you into judgment.
verses.textEnNlt: Young people, it’s wonderful to be young! Enjoy every minute of it. Do everything you want to do; take it all in. But remember that you must give an account to God for everything you do.
verses.textEnNasb: Rejoice, young man, during your childhood, and let your heart be pleasant during the days of young manhood. And follow the impulses of your heart and the desires of your eyes. Yet know that God will bring you to judgment for all these things.
verses.textEn: You who are young, be happy while you are young, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Follow the ways of your heart and whatever your eyes see, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

verses.textZh: 所以你当除掉心中的烦恼，除去肉体的疾苦，因为无论是幼年或是壮年，都是虚空的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 所以你当除掉心中的烦恼，除去肉体的疾苦，因为无论是幼年或是壮年，都是虚空的。
verses.textZhCuv: 所以，你当从心中除掉愁烦，从肉体克去邪恶；因为一生的开端和幼年之时，都是虚空的。
verses.textEnNiv: So then, banish anxiety from your heart and cast off the troubles of your body, for youth and vigor are meaningless.
verses.textEnEsv: Remove vexation from your heart, and put away pain from your body, for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, And put away evil from your flesh, For childhood and youth are vanity.
verses.textEnNlt: So refuse to worry, and keep your body healthy. But remember that youth, with a whole life before you, is meaningless.
verses.textEnNasb: So remove sorrow from your heart and keep pain away from your body, because childhood and the prime of life are fleeting.
verses.textEn: So then, banish anxiety from your heart and cast off the troubles of your body, for youth and vigor are meaningless.

verses.textZh: 在你壮年的日子，当记念你的创造主。不要等到衰败的日子，就是你所说："我毫无喜乐"的那些年日临到，
verses.textZhCnvs: 在你壮年的日子，当记念你的创造主。不要等到衰败的日子，就是你所说："我毫无喜乐"的那些年日临到，
verses.textZhCuv: 你趁着年幼、衰败的日子尚未来到，就是你所说，我毫无喜乐的那些年日未曾临近之先，当记念造你的主。
verses.textEnNiv: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years approach when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them"—
verses.textEnEsv: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years draw near of which you will say, "I have no pleasure in them";
verses.textEnNkjv: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, Before the difficult days come, And the years draw near when you say, "I have no pleasure in them":
verses.textEnNlt: Don’t let the excitement of youth cause you to forget your Creator. Honor him in your youth before you grow old and say, "Life is not pleasant anymore."
verses.textEnNasb: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years approach when you will say, "I have no pleasure in them";
verses.textEn: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years approach when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them"—

verses.textZh: 日头、光明、月亮、星宿变暗，雨后乌云再现的时候。
verses.textZhCnvs: 日头、光明、月亮、星宿变暗，雨后乌云再现的时候。
verses.textZhCuv: 不要等到日头、光明、月亮、星宿变为黑暗，雨后云彩反回，
verses.textEnNiv: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.textEnEsv: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are darkened and the clouds return after the rain,
verses.textEnNkjv: While the sun and the light, The moon and the stars, Are not darkened, And the clouds do not return after the rain;
verses.textEnNlt: Remember him before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is dim to your old eyes, and rain clouds continually darken your sky.
verses.textEnNasb: before the sun and the light, the moon and the stars are darkened, and clouds return after the rain;
verses.textEn: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;

verses.textZh: 那时，看守房子的发抖，强壮的弯腰，推磨的稀少，都停了工，往窗外看的都昏暗了，
verses.textZhCnvs: 那时，看守房子的发抖，强壮的弯腰，推磨的稀少，都停了工，往窗外看的都昏暗了，
verses.textZhCuv: 看守房屋的发颤，有力的屈身，推磨的稀少就止息，从窗户往外看的都昏暗；
verses.textEnNiv: when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking through the windows grow dim;
verses.textEnEsv: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men are bent, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows are dimmed,
verses.textEnNkjv: In the day when the keepers of the house tremble, And the strong men bow down; When the grinders cease because they are few, And those that look through the windows grow dim;
verses.textEnNlt: Remember him before your legs—the guards of your house—start to tremble; and before your shoulders—the strong men—stoop. Remember him before your teeth—your few remaining servants—stop grinding; and before your eyes—the women looking through the windows—see dimly.
verses.textEnNasb: on the day that the watchmen of the house tremble, and strong men are bent over, the grinders stop working because they are few, and those who look through windows grow dim;
verses.textEn: when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men stoop, when the grinders cease because they are few, and those looking through the windows grow dim;

verses.textZh: 当街的门口关闭，推磨的声音微弱。雀鸟一叫，人就起来。唱歌的歌声 都低微。
verses.textZhCnvs: 当街的门口关闭，推磨的声音微弱。雀鸟一叫，人就起来。唱歌的歌声 都低微。
verses.textZhCuv: 街门关闭，推磨的响声微小，雀鸟一叫，人就起来，唱歌的女子也都衰微。
verses.textEnNiv: when the doors to the street are closed and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise up at the sound of birds, but all their songs grow faint;
verses.textEnEsv: and the doors on the street are shut—when the sound of the grinding is low, and one rises up at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low—
verses.textEnNkjv: When the doors are shut in the streets, And the sound of grinding is low; When one rises up at the sound of a bird, And all the daughters of music are brought low.
verses.textEnNlt: Remember him before the door to life’s opportunities is closed and the sound of work fades. Now you rise at the first chirping of the birds, but then all their sounds will grow faint.
verses.textEnNasb: and the doors on the street are shut as the sound of the grinding mill is low, and one will arise at the sound of the bird, and all the daughters of song will sing softly.
verses.textEn: when the doors to the street are closed and the sound of grinding fades; when people rise up at the sound of birds, but all their songs grow faint;

verses.textZh: 人怕高处，怕路上有惊吓。杏树开花，蚱蜢蹒跚而行，催情果失效。因为人归他永远的家，哭丧的在街上游行。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人怕高处，怕路上有惊吓。杏树开花，蚱蜢蹒跚而行，催情果失效。因为人归他永远的家，哭丧的在街上游行。
verses.textZhCuv: 人怕高处，路上有惊慌，杏树开花，蚱蜢成为重担，人所愿的也都废掉；因为人归他永远的家，吊丧的在街上往来。
verses.textEnNiv: when people are afraid of heights and of dangers in the streets; when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags itself along and desire no longer is stirred. Then people go to their eternal home and mourners go about the streets.
verses.textEnEsv: they are afraid also of what is high, and terrors are in the way; the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire fails, because man is going to his eternal home, and the mourners go about the streets—
verses.textEnNkjv: Also they are afraid of height, And of terrors in the way; When the almond tree blossoms, The grasshopper is a burden, And desire fails. For man goes to his eternal home, And the mourners go about the streets.
verses.textEnNlt: Remember him before you become fearful of falling and worry about danger in the streets; before your hair turns white like an almond tree in bloom, and you drag along without energy like a dying grasshopper, and the caperberry no longer inspires sexual desire. Remember him before you near the grave, your everlasting home, when the mourners will weep at your funeral.
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, people are afraid of a high place and of terrors on the road; the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry is ineffective. For man goes to his eternal home while the mourners move around in the street.
verses.textEn: when people are afraid of heights and of dangers in the streets; when the almond tree blossoms and the grasshopper drags itself along and desire no longer is stirred. Then people go to their eternal home and mourners go about the streets.

verses.textZh: 银炼断掉，金碗破裂，瓶子在泉旁破碎，打水的轮子在井边破烂。
verses.textZhCnvs: 银炼断掉，金碗破裂，瓶子在泉旁破碎，打水的轮子在井边破烂。
verses.textZhCuv: 银链折断，金罐破裂，瓶子在泉旁损坏，水轮在井口破烂，
verses.textEnNiv: Remember him—before the silver cord is severed, and the golden bowl is broken; before the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel broken at the well,
verses.textEnEsv: before the silver cord is snapped, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is shattered at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
verses.textEnNkjv: RememberyourCreator before the silver cord is loosed, Or the golden bowl is broken, Or the pitcher shattered at the fountain, Or the wheel broken at the well.
verses.textEnNlt: Yes, remember your Creator now while you are young, before the silver cord of life snaps and the golden bowl is broken. Don’t wait until the water jar is smashed at the spring and the pulley is broken at the well.
verses.textEnNasb: Remember your Creator before the silver cord is broken and the golden bowl is crushed, the pitcher by the spring is shattered and the wheel at the cistern is crushed;
verses.textEn: Remember him—before the silver cord is severed, and the golden bowl is broken; before the pitcher is shattered at the spring, and the wheel broken at the well,

verses.textZh: 尘土要归回原来之地，灵要归回赐灵的神。
verses.textZhCnvs: 尘土要归回原来之地，灵要归回赐灵的神。
verses.textZhCuv: 尘土仍归于地，灵仍归于赐灵的神。
verses.textEnNiv: and the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.textEnEsv: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the dust will return to the earth as it was, And the spirit will return to God who gave it.
verses.textEnNlt: For then the dust will return to the earth, and the spirit will return to God who gave it.
verses.textEnNasb: then the dust will return to the earth as it was, and the spirit will return to God who gave it.
verses.textEn: and the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

verses.textZh: 传道者说："虚空的虚空，一切都是虚空。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 传道者说："虚空的虚空，一切都是虚空。"
verses.textZhCuv: 传道者说：「虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。」
verses.textEnNiv: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"
verses.textEnEsv: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher; all is vanity.
verses.textEnNkjv: "Vanity of vanities," says the Preacher, "All is vanity."
verses.textEnNlt: "Everything is meaningless," says the Teacher, "completely meaningless."
verses.textEnNasb: "Futility of futilities," says the Preacher, "all is futility!"
verses.textEn: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Everything is meaningless!"

verses.textZh: 传道者不但有智慧，还将知识教训众人；他既揣摩，又查考，也编撰了许多箴言。
verses.textZhCnvs: 传道者不但有智慧，还将知识教训众人；他既揣摩，又查考，也编撰了许多箴言。
verses.textZhCuv: 再者，传道者因有智慧，仍将知识教训众人；又默想，又考查，又陈说许多箴言。
verses.textEnNiv: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also imparted knowledge to the people. He pondered and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
verses.textEnEsv: Besides being wise, the Preacher also taught the people knowledge, weighing and studying and arranging many proverbs with great care.
verses.textEnNkjv: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yes, he pondered and sought out and set in order many proverbs.
verses.textEnNlt: Keep this in mind: The Teacher was considered wise, and he taught the people everything he knew. He listened carefully to many proverbs, studying and classifying them.
verses.textEnNasb: In addition to being wise, the Preacher also taught the people knowledge; and he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
verses.textEn: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also imparted knowledge to the people. He pondered and searched out and set in order many proverbs.

verses.textZh: 传道者搜寻可喜悦的话，正确地写下真理。
verses.textZhCnvs: 传道者搜寻可喜悦的话，正确地写下真理。
verses.textZhCuv: 传道者专心寻求可喜悦的言语，是凭正直写的诚实话。
verses.textEnNiv: The Teacher searched to find just the right words, and what he wrote was upright and true.
verses.textEnEsv: The Preacher sought to find words of delight, and uprightly he wrote words of truth.
verses.textEnNkjv: The Preacher sought to find acceptable words; and whatwas written was upright—words of truth.
verses.textEnNlt: The Teacher sought to find just the right words to express truths clearly.
verses.textEnNasb: The Preacher sought to find delightful words and to write words of truth correctly.
verses.textEn: The Teacher searched to find just the right words, and what he wrote was upright and true.

verses.textZh: 智慧人的言语像刺棒，他们所汇集的箴言像钉牢的钉子，都是一位牧者所赐的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 智慧人的言语像刺棒，他们所汇集的箴言像钉牢的钉子，都是一位牧者所赐的。
verses.textZhCuv: 智慧人的言语好像刺棍；会中之师的言语又像钉稳的钉子，都是一个牧者所赐的。
verses.textEnNiv: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails—given by one shepherd.
verses.textEnEsv: The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails firmly fixed are the collected sayings; they are given by one Shepherd.
verses.textEnNkjv: The words of the wise are like goads, and the words of scholars are like well-driven nails, given by one Shepherd.
verses.textEnNlt: The words of the wise are like cattle prods—painful but helpful. Their collected sayings are like a nail-studded stick with which a shepherd drives the sheep.
verses.textEnNasb: The words of the wise are like goads, and masters of these collections are like driven nails; they are given by one Shepherd.
verses.textEn: The words of the wise are like goads, their collected sayings like firmly embedded nails—given by one shepherd.

verses.textZh: 我儿，还有，你当受劝勉：著书多，没有穷尽；读书多，身体疲倦。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我儿，还有，你当受劝勉：著书多，没有穷尽；读书多，身体疲倦。
verses.textZhCuv: 我儿，还有一层，你当受劝戒：著书多，没有穷尽；读书多，身体疲倦。
verses.textEnNiv: Be warned, my son, of anything in addition to them. Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.
verses.textEnEsv: My son, beware of anything beyond these. Of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
verses.textEnNkjv: And further, my son, be admonished by these. Of making many books thereis no end, and much study is wearisome to the flesh.
verses.textEnNlt: But, my child, let me give you some further advice: Be careful, for writing books is endless, and much study wears you out.
verses.textEnNasb: But beyond this, my son, be warned: the writing of many books is endless, and excessive study is wearying to the body.
verses.textEn: Be warned, my son, of anything in addition to them. Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.

verses.textZh: 你们一切都听见了，总而言之，应当敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，因为这是每一个人的本分。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你们一切都听见了，总而言之，应当敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，因为这是每一个人的本分。
verses.textZhCuv: 这些事都已听见了，总意就是：敬畏神，谨守他的诫命，这是人所当尽的本分 。
verses.textEnNiv: Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the duty of all mankind.
verses.textEnEsv: The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.textEnNkjv: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God and keep His commandments, For this is man’s all.
verses.textEnNlt: That’s the whole story. Here now is my final conclusion: Fear God and obey his commands, for this is everyone’s duty.
verses.textEnNasb: The conclusion, when everything has been heard, is: fear God and keep His commandments, because this applies to every person.
verses.textEn: Now all has been heard; here is the conclusion of the matter: Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the duty of all mankind.

verses.textZh: 人所作的每一件事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人所作的每一件事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。
verses.textZhCuv: 因为人所做的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，神都必审问。
verses.textEnNiv: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
verses.textEnEsv: For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil.
verses.textEnNkjv: For God will bring every work into judgment, Including every secret thing, Whether good or evil.
verses.textEnNlt: God will judge us for everything we do, including every secret thing, whether good or bad.
verses.textEnNasb: For God will bring every act to judgment, everything which is hidden, whether it is good or evil.
verses.textEn: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether it is good or evil.
